paragraphs.text: The book declares that Moses was "the servant of the Lord" so that the people would not regard him as a god because of his greatness. Likewise it calls Joshua "Moses' minister", and this is for two reasons:
1- The humility of Joshua, the writer of the book, who does not call himself the head or the leader; this protects him from pride.

2- A declaration that he is bound by all the teachings of God which were delivered to Moses, so that he is Moses' natural continuation. These verses show the role of God in the people's receiving of their inheritance, which points to the salvation of mankind and their receiving of their heavenly portion. Moses points to the Law, which does not bring mankind to heaven but promises them that, and then hands the leadership over to Joshua, who is a symbol of Christ, who gives us eternal life.

The servant dies, but the service continues, and someone is urgently needed to lead it after Moses. The divine command comes to Joshua, who was still affected by the death of Moses, to take up the leadership, and to do so immediately, "now", at the time when the Jordan was in its season of flooding (the time of harvest) (ch. 3:15, 16). How could Joshua cross with all the people, their women, their children and their belongings, a flooded and violently flowing river, with no crossing (bridge) or boats for passage?!

The name Jordan means "descender", since its rate of descent equals 30 times the descent of the Nile, which makes the crossing even harder; yet the promise of the Lord to His people must be fulfilled.

Now God fulfills His promise to Moses to give the people the Promised Land (Num 13:1, Deut 11:24), and also fulfills His promises to the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob. God promises His people that every place that the sole of their foot shall tread upon will be theirs, and this means:
1- The unlimited love of God for His people, that they may take as much of the land as they are able.
2- The importance of spiritual striving for obtaining the grace of God.
3- It signifies the spiritual man who treads upon earthly desires as much as he is able, and so receives countless heavenly blessings.

God says in the past tense, "have I given unto you", although they did not yet possess it, because it is in the heart of God to give it to them, and so it is a settled matter that must come to pass; that is, God's promise to them is sure.
Your coast: your borders.

The Hittites: they are the sons of Heth, son of Canaan, son of Ham (Gen 10:15), and they represent the strongest of the Canaanite peoples. Their country extended through Palestine, northern Syria, northern Iraq and Asia Minor, that is, Turkey. The children of Israel took possession of some of their lands but did not possess the rest, because of their negligence in carrying out God's commandments to drive out the wicked and cleanse the land. The Hittites fought many wars with Egypt, the strongest nation at that time.

The Lord shows the borders of the land: the Arabian desert and the wilderness of Sinai to the south, Lebanon to the north, the river Euphrates, which is 2,850 kilometers long, to the east, and the Mediterranean Sea to the west. Thus the wilderness, which signifies spiritual drought, and the world with its salt water, which the Mediterranean Sea signifies, remain outside the borders. This area includes the land of the Hittites and other Canaanites. The Hittites were mentioned specifically because they were the strongest of the peoples in this region, to support His people and to confirm their faith and their ability to possess the Promised Land, even the regions in which the strong peoples dwell.

He promises Joshua that none of these pagan peoples, whose land they were entering to possess, would be able to stand before him; rather, all would submit to him, and he would defeat them and drive them out. Just as God supported Moses, so He supports Joshua.
God also encouraged Joshua that he would possess this land which he was entering and divide it among the tribes of the children of Israel, as He promised the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.

God is the One who takes the initiative to push us along the way of our salvation with support, encouragement and companionship. So do not fear failure and do not turn back, but complete the way by His strength.
Only: all you have to do is ...
To the right hand or to the left: the right signifies excess and exaggeration, and the left signifies neglect, deficiency and carelessness. Prosper: succeed.

God tells Joshua, as a servant responsible for leading his people, that his duty is to be steadfast in faith and courageous, however strong the enemies who face him. What is required of him is not any material strength but holding fast, with all exactness, to the law of God which Moses taught him, and so he will be assured of success in his wars and in all his works.
Meditate: keep the words and repeat them so that they remain in your mind.

He stresses to him the importance of holding fast to the word of God, so that he understands it, keeps it and repeats it throughout the day and even in the night, and does not turn aside from it, and then it corrects his errors and makes him succeed in all his life.

Because of the difficulty of confronting the many nations dwelling in the land of Canaan, God encourages Joshua for the third time and supports him, so that he would not fear their strength but rely on the command of God and His promise to be with him.

Take care to read the word of God, to meditate on it, to memorize it and to repeat it throughout your day in the form of a verse or a psalm, so that you may feel the presence of God with you and rely on Him, and even delight in fellowship with Him. Then you will rejoice even in the midst of difficult circumstances and pass through them reassured, because God is with you.
Officers: the civil leaders of the children of Israel.
Host: the place where they pitch their tents and dwell.

Joshua commanded the officers of the people to pass through the midst of them to alert them, to have them prepare to enter the Promised Land, and to prepare the food and drink needed for this long journey, whose extent was not known, because they were entering among people who were strangers to them, whom they would fight and drive out of their land because of their wickedness. This provision they took from the plants and produce of the land east of the Jordan, where the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh dwelt. Here appears the importance of human spiritual striving, which is supported by divine grace: they do what they are able to do by taking provision, and God completes His grace by their victory over the enemies.

Do everything you are able to do to show your love for God by holding fast to your prayers, your readings and your service of others; and on the other hand, avoid the sources of evil and keep away from every sin, and God will support you and make you prosper in all your ways.
Beyond Jordan toward the sunrising: the eastern bank of the river Jordan.

Joshua reminded the men of the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh of the command of Moses to them: that after they possessed their land east of the Jordan and built houses for their wives and children and folds for their livestock, they were to go forward before their brethren to fight the enemies and drive them out of their land west of the Jordan, and then, after the war was completed and all the tribes had possessed the new land and settled in it, they would return to their places east of the Jordan (Num 32).

The tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh agreed to the commands Joshua gave them, and they also promised to obey him in everything as they had obeyed Moses. The third thing they promised was their readiness to punish with death anyone who disobeyed his words, so that they would not trouble him in his leading of them and in confronting the enemies. And the fourth thing is that they encouraged him to carry out his duties of leadership.
Rahab and the spies

entries.section: (1) The two spies in the house of Rahab

paragraphs.text: Shittim: plural of shittah, that is, the acacia tree; it is the name of a place that was full of acacia trees, located in the land of Moab east of the river Jordan near where it meets the Dead Sea, where the people were staying (Num 25:1). Rahab: a woman's name meaning a broad or wide place.

Jericho: it means "fragrance"; it is the name of a city that had an abundance of balsam plants that gave it a sweet fragrance. It is located west of the river Jordan opposite Shittim, about five miles from the river and about 17 miles north-east of Jerusalem. It is a fortified city in a valley and surrounded by fertile land (Map 1). Lebanon Mediterranean Sea Syria Hazor Sea of Galilee Mount Ebal Mount Gerizim Shechem Jordan River Jordan Shiloh Ai Gilgal Gibeon Shittim Jericho Valley of Aijalon Jerusalem Hebron Dead Sea Moab Map (1) In complete secrecy, Joshua sent two spies to study the nature of the land, the site, and the city of Jericho and its fortifications, because it was the first city that Joshua would fight in the Promised Land. Secrecy was necessary to preserve the lives of the two spies. Spying was a necessity before fighting any city.

Jericho lies at the entrance of passes between the mountains that lead to the surrounding lands such as Ai and Jerusalem. Joshua, by God's guidance, chose to enter at Jericho and did not enter from the south of Palestine, because the land there is fortified, and so that none of the surrounding nations, such as Egypt and the land of the Arabs, would attack him. Had they entered from the south, Egypt might have risen to resist the attackers, because the south of Palestine is east of the wilderness of Sinai, which belonged to Egypt.

It is likely that Rahab rented out her house, part of which she lived in with her family, as an inn for strangers. She also worked in one of the pagan temples as a harlot, since fornication was one of the practices of pagan worship to which Rahab had vowed herself; therefore the temples had male and female prostitutes so that the worshippers might fulfill their vows with them by fornication. This shows us how corrupt the Canaanite pagan worship was at that time, which led God to issue His command to kill many of these corrupt pagans, who deserved death because of the multitude of their evils, and for fear that their bad customs would pass to the Jewish people if they mingled with them.
The two spies lodged at Rahab's inn so that none of the inhabitants of Jericho would suspect them, since many people frequented this house for fornication or lodging.
The two spies symbolize the apostles of Christ in the sending out of the Twelve and then the sending out of the Seventy, or the disciples sent out two by two to preach.

entries.section: (1) The two spies in the house of Rahab

paragraphs.text: The men told the king of Jericho what had happened, especially since the city was tense and awaiting an attack on it by the Jews, and it was easy to detect the entry of strangers into a limited city like Jericho. The king of Jericho symbolizes the man who resists God.

entries.section: (1) The two spies in the house of Rahab

paragraphs.text: The king asked Rahab to hand over the two men, but she was not willing; rather, she denied that she knew they were Jewish spies, although it will become clear from the rest of the account that she was lying. Lying is approved by Rahab's religion, but it is not approved by Christianity, whatever its reason. Rahab lied because she had heard of the power of the God of the children of Israel and had begun to believe in Him, and she desired to please Him and to take refuge in Him.

entries.section: (1) The two spies in the house of Rahab

paragraphs.text: Rahab misled the king's messengers, telling them that the two men had left before dark, because the gates of Jericho were shut at nightfall like all cities, and that she did not know where they had gone, so the messengers hurried away to search for them as Rahab had instructed them.

entries.section: (1) The two spies in the house of Rahab

paragraphs.text: Laid in order: placed one upon another in an arrangement.

After that she brought them up to the roof of her house, where she had laid some stalks of flax to dry after washing, so that they could be combed and turned into threads for weaving, and she hid the two spies under the stalks of flax.

Perhaps the flax under which the two spies hid, from which the priestly garments were made in the law of Moses, points to the intercession and work of the priesthood, which hides us in the blessing of the Holy Sacraments, so that we escape the pursuit of Satan.

entries.section: (1) The two spies in the house of Rahab

paragraphs.text: The fords: plural of ford, which is a shallow place where people cross the river by wading through the water on foot.

The guards went toward the fords of the Jordan, thinking that the two spies would cross the river there to return to Joshua. And since the city gate was shut as every day, it would be easy to catch the two spies if they were still inside the city.

The love of God is wonderful in His protection of the two spies, not through friends of theirs, but through a woman of a foreign race and notorious for evil. So do not be troubled, for you are in a faithful hand, the hand of God, which protects you wherever you go and gives you favor in the eyes of those from whom you do not expect it.
Sea of Suph: the Red Sea.
Utterly destroyed: killed.

After that Rahab told the two spies that she knew that the God of the children of Israel was mighty and would give them the land of the Canaanites, so that everyone was in terror, especially from knowing of the miracle of the Lord's dividing of the Red Sea by the hand of Moses and the drowning of Pharaoh, and then of their victory over the two kings of the Amorites on the way and their killing of them (Deut 2, 3). Rahab had learned these reports through the trade caravans and travelers, especially since she hosted strangers to stay in her house, so that much news of the world around her reached her. What Rahab said declares her faith in God, the God of Israel, as the New Testament testifies to this in (Heb 11:31, Jas 2:25).

If the people of God perished in the wilderness through their unbelief in Him and their disobedience to Him in entering the Promised Land, yet Rahab, the Gentile harlot, when she believed in God, prophesied of the children of Israel's taking possession of the land, and God saved her and her household from death, and she even became a grandmother of Christ. So believe in God so that you may enjoy His work in you. Seek Him earnestly, confident of His love, whatever the adverse circumstances around you and whatever your weakness or your sins.
Melted: feared greatly.

Rahab confessed her faith in the one God, the King of heaven and earth, and asked them to deal kindly with her and to confirm that by swearing by the name of the Lord, in return for her kindness to them. This would be by giving her a sign or proposing a plan so that she and all her family would escape death when the people arrived at the city and conquered it.

The two men assured her that they were responsible for her life and that of her household, since they would deal kindly with her in return for her hiding them, so that they would not die with the inhabitants of Jericho.
The window: the casement.

Since her house was adjoining the wall of the city, she let them down by a rope through the window of her house, whose wall is the wall of the city, because they could not go out by the closed gates, which were guarded by the king's agents.
The pursuers: the king's men whom he sent to run after the two spies and catch them.

She told them to go toward the mountains between Jericho and Jerusalem, that is, opposite to the direction of the river Jordan which they had crossed when they came to Jericho, and she told them to hide from those who were searching for them in the mountain for three days, which was the expected length of the search, and then to turn back and cross the Jordan to Joshua.
Scarlet: dark red.

The two spies set a sign for Rahab so that the Jewish attackers would know her house when they attacked Jericho, and it was to hang a scarlet-colored cord in the window of her house adjoining the wall. They commanded her to gather her father, her mother and all her household inside her house so that they would not die, and if she did not fulfill this condition, the attackers would not know her and her family, and they would be exposed to death. Therefore the two spies said to her that we are blameless of our oath to you to preserve the life of you and your family if you do not fulfill this condition.

The scarlet color signifies the blood of Christ, which is a condition for obtaining salvation, and the house of Rahab signifies the Church, in which the believers take refuge; for without the Church and its sacraments and the means of grace within it, we do not obtain salvation.

The two spies set two conditions for salvation by this sign: the first is the commitment to remain inside the house, because there is no salvation outside the Church, and whoever goes out is responsible for the destruction that befalls him.

The second condition is to keep the matter secret from the king, lest he destroy the two spies, and this is an indication of the necessity of our faithfulness to Christ, that we not betray Him, so that He may allow us to enjoy His salvation.
Then they departed, and she put the scarlet cord in the window. This shows her faith, which made her hang the scarlet cord after the two spies left her house.

The two spies hid in the mountain for three days as she had told them, and then returned to Joshua and told him all that had happened and of the terror of the inhabitants of the land because of the Jewish people, because everyone was certain of the power of the God of the children of Israel.

The words of the two spies show their strong faith in the power of God, who would give them the land of Canaan, for they said, "Truly the Lord hath delivered into our hands all the land"; and this is the opposite of the ten spies in their unbelief long ago in the days of Moses, because of which all the people died in the wilderness of Sinai and did not enter the Promised Land.

Although the two spies relied on God's protection of them, they acted with wisdom and hid for three days. May you be faithful in performing your duties and act with wisdom in every situation, according to what God guides you and those who love you advise you, and so enjoy God's care; for He does not love the lazy and the negligent, but He keeps and saves the weak and the humble who are faithful in their works.
Crossing the Jordan
The morrow: that is, the morrow of the eighth day, which is the ninth day.

The people moved under the leadership of Joshua from Shittim on the ninth day of Nisan and reached the river Jordan after they had prepared provision for the way (ch. 1:10, 11), and they lodged one night at the Jordan, because their crossing of the river was on the tenth day of Nisan (ch. 4:19).

Three days after the return of the two spies, who returned on the sixth day of Nisan, the officers, that is, the leaders of the people, went through the midst of them, that is, on the ninth day of Nisan, one day before they crossed the river Jordan.

The leaders commanded the people to move behind the ark of the covenant of the Lord, which the priests of the tribe of Levi were carrying. The ark went before the people, making them feel the presence of God who was leading them, so that they would not fear the enemies. This time the priests carried the ark themselves and not the Levites (Num 4:15), because of the seriousness of the situation and to encourage the people.

The leaders also commanded the people that there should be a distance between them and the ark of the covenant going before them, which is two thousand cubits, that is, about one kilometer, for the following reasons:
1- That they might feel the fear of God, and so look upon it from afar and be reverent before Him.

2- The existence of a great distance, which is a kilometer, makes the ark clear before the eyes of all the people, so that it leads them easily and they remember that God is their leader in their new life in the Promised Land. This signifies the leading of the Lord for us in life to the new Canaan, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

3- There was a great distance between the ark and them to declare that the Law in the Old Testament gives us the fear of God and prepares us for life with Him, but in the New Testament we draw near to the Holy of Holies and partake of the Body and Blood of the Lord.

4- The ark of the covenant contained the Ten Commandments, that is, the word of God that leads us in the way of life with Him. It was called the ark of the covenant of the Lord so that they would remember their covenant with the Lord to obey His commandments, and then He would keep them, strengthen them and give them victory over their enemies.
Sanctify yourselves: by bathing, washing the clothes, abstaining from marital relations, together with repentance of heart and leaving every sin.
Joshua commanded the people to sanctify themselves spiritually and bodily in preparation for witnessing the great work of God in their crossing of the river Jordan.
Then Joshua commanded the priests to take up the ark of the covenant of the Lord and pass over before the people, and they did so on the morning of the tenth day of the month of Nisan.
May God be a leader for you in the course of your life, so that you remember Him at the beginning of every day as your only goal and seek Him before any work, that He may guide you in all your steps.

God declared to Joshua that He would show His greatness before the people as He had magnified Moses before. The beginning of Joshua's magnifying is the dividing of the river Jordan by the hand of Joshua and the crossing of the people, and then He will magnify him after that in his victory over the peoples of the land of Canaan and his dividing of their lands among the tribes of the children of Israel.

Joshua commanded the priests who bore the ark that when they reached the river and their feet touched the water, they were to stand still there, because the waters would withdraw from beneath their feet and the river Jordan would be divided, as will come in (v. 15).
The Canaanites: the inhabitants of the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, from the descendants of Canaan.
The Hittites: a strong people from the descendants of Canaan, whose land was north of Palestine between the Euphrates and Lebanon.
The Hivites: from the descendants of Ham, who dwell in cities and work in trade.
The Perizzites: from the inhabitants of villages and deserts, who work in farming or herding.
The Girgashites: the inhabitants east of the Sea of Galilee.
The Amorites: they dwell in the mountains east of the Jordan and are a strong people.
The Jebusites: the ancient inhabitants of Jerusalem and its surroundings.

Joshua assured them that God would drive out the pagan peoples from before them, because their leader was God, who appeared before them in the ark of His covenant, and God is the God of gods and the Lord of all the earth, so the gods of the nations, who are demons, cannot stand before Him.

Let us rejoice that we have from the Lord a promise of the inheritance of the Kingdom, which He will fulfill for us however long the time, according to His true promise. Let us cast away from us every sin or desire, however attractive, and not be troubled if we fall, but rise quickly, confident of God's love for us in preparing the eternal inheritance so that we may reign with Him.
A heap: it stands like a wall or a rampart.

Joshua commanded the people to choose one man from each tribe for a task that would be announced later, and he told them that when the feet of the priests who bore the ark touched the waters of the river, the waters coming from the north, that is, from the side of the source, would stop in one high heap and become like a wall of water, while the rest of the waters flowing toward their outlet in the Dead Sea continued to withdraw on their way, and so the bed of the river Jordan became dry ground over which all the people crossed.
His banks: the shores of the river Jordan and its embankments.

So it happened as the Lord promised, and the time was the season of the river's flooding from the melting of the snows of the mountains of Lebanon, which makes the river wide and violent in its flow, and this was at the time of the days of the barley harvest at the end of winter.

Adam: the name of a city beside Zaretan, 25 kilometers north of Jericho (Map 1). The sea of the plain: the salt sea, which is the Dead Sea, into which the river Jordan flows from the north. The flow of water in the river Jordan stopped at the city of Adam, which is beside the city of Zaretan, and these are 25 km north of Jericho and of the place where the children of Israel were gathered east of the Jordan. The waters withdrew toward their outlet in the Dead Sea, and the bed of the Jordan became uncovered without water, and all the people crossed from their place, which was later called Bethabara (Jn 1:28), because from it the children of Israel crossed and reached the western side that is called Gilgal (ch. 4:19), and by this they were five miles from the city of Jericho.

It is noticed that in the crossing of the Red Sea the waters stood to the right and to the left and the people crossed between them (Ex 14:22), but here the waters stood like a wall on one side only, which is the north side.

After the land dried up before the children of Israel and the priests bearing the ark of the covenant of the Lord entered into the midst of the river Jordan, all the people passed over and crossed from the east of the Jordan to its west. Two things are noticed in this:

1- The priests did not come out of the river until they were assured that all the people had crossed. This is the duty of the priests in both Testaments, namely caring for the people, baptizing them in the baptismal font, and watching over their walk in the new life.

2- The people crossed the Red Sea forty years before, and those who crossed died, and that crossing was a symbol of Baptism. Now the new generation crosses the river Jordan, which also signifies Baptism, before their entering the new land. Likewise, the sacrament of Baptism is the entrance to all the sacraments and to life in the Church.

God chose the time of the flooding of the river Jordan not only to show His miracle in stopping the overflowing waters so that His people might cross, but also because at this time no one expects a great people like this to cross, so their attack on the city of Jericho was a surprise; for in the other days of the year there may be times when the waters of the Jordan are low, so that an ordinary person can cross in water that reaches his knees or a little more.

God is able to remove every obstacle from your path, as He stopped the waters in the river Jordan so that His people might cross. So do not be troubled by hindrances, however great, but persevere in prayer and do faithfully all that is in your power, and God is able to remove all obstacles, even if they have lasted a long time, and bring you to the salvation of your soul.
Coming up out of the river Jordan

After all the people had crossed, the Lord asked Joshua to command twelve men representing the tribes to take twelve stones from beneath the feet of the priests bearing the ark in the midst of the Jordan, and to carry them with them and place them on the western bank of the river Jordan, where they would lodge that night. The twelve men are the number of the tribes of the children of Israel, so that all the tribes might share in glorifying God, who worked with them the miracle of the crossing of the Jordan. The number "12" is also the number of the disciples of Christ, so it signifies the Church in the Old and New Testaments. The number "12" is the product of the number "3", which signifies the Holy Trinity and its work in the believers, and the number "4", which signifies the four directions of the world, that is, the believers in every place; so the number "12" signifies holiness in all the believers.
Before the ark of the Lord: that is, toward the ark.
In time to come: in the future.
What mean ye by these stones?: what is the reason for the presence of these stones.

Joshua commanded the twelve men, whom he had chosen from the twelve tribes, to go into the depth of the Jordan, that is, to the ark which the priests were carrying, and take from there twelve stones and transfer them to the western bank of the river Jordan and set them up there as a memorial of the miracle of the crossing of the Jordan, to be a witness to this miracle, and so that the fathers might teach it to their children to strengthen their faith in God.

Joshua commanded the people to tell their children the story of the miracle of their crossing of the river Jordan when they asked them about the stone monument made of the twelve stones on the western bank of the Jordan in the place where they lodged, which was called Gilgal (v. 19). After that the chosen men took the twelve stones from the bed of the Jordan and placed them in the place where they lodged on the western bank.
Joshua set up twelve stones, which the men had lifted from the western bank of the Jordan, and fixed them in the bed of the river.

Do not find the toil of spiritual striving burdensome, whether to rid yourself of your sins or to acquire virtues and persevere in spiritual practices, because this gives you life with God and you enjoy fellowship with Him.

The priests who bore the ark remained in the bed of the river Jordan until the chosen men had lifted the stones to the western bank and buried stones in their place in the bottom of the river, and until Joshua had finished charging the people to teach their children as Moses had commanded him before his death, passing on the word of God which He taught Moses. The people crossed the Jordan quickly for the following reasons:
1- Joshua had commanded this so that they would feel seriousness and zeal and begin their new life in the new land with energy.
2- They were eager to reach the new land and possess it.
3- Because their number was large, about 2 million, and with them were children.
The priests themselves did not cross until they were assured of the crossing of all the people, confirming the fatherhood of the priest and his concern for all his people.
Armed: prepared with weapons of war.
Before the children of Israel: going ahead, the men of war from the rest of the tribes.

Soldiers also crossed from the two and a half tribes who had received their portion of the land east of the Jordan, to fight with their brethren as the Lord asked of them by the mouth of Moses (Num 32, ch. 1:16-18).
Prepared for war: ready for battle.
The plains of Jericho: the flat lands of Jericho.

The number of those who crossed from the two and a half tribes was about forty thousand persons, to take part in the holy wars west of the Jordan, which the Lord leads. This number is about half the number of the soldiers of the two and a half tribes, whose number is estimated in the text at 110,580 persons, and it is clear that the rest remained in the land east of the Jordan to guard the women, the children and the possessions. All of them encamped in the plains of Jericho.

If God is concerned to glorify His holy children, this calls us to glorify them, because glorifying them is glorifying God Himself. So take care to remember your intercessor and glorify him on his feast day and at all times, so that you may learn something from him and God may rejoice in your love for Him.
By this the Lord confirmed the greatness of Joshua and the Lord's support of him before all the people, so they respected him as their leader in place of Moses all the days of his life.
The ark of the testimony: the ark of the covenant, with the two tablets of the commandments in it.

After all the people had crossed the Jordan, the priests bearing the ark came up as the Lord commanded, and the waters returned to flowing and the river filled to its fullest extent. This signifies that the person who submits to the Church and its priests is protected by God from many dangers in the world, but if he moves away from the Church, problems close in on him like the waters of the Jordan, which returned to their flow.

The children of Israel came up and crossed the Jordan on the tenth day of the month of Nisan, and by this they completed forty years less five days since they crossed the Red Sea, which they crossed on the fifteenth day of the month of Nisan. They reached Gilgal, whose name means rolling or rolled away, and Joshua called it by this name because God rolled away from them the reproach of Egypt and they arrived at settlement in the Promised Land. Gilgal is located west of the river Jordan beside Jericho and east of it (Map 1).
As for the stones that Joshua took from the bed of the river, he set them up in Gilgal, to which they had crossed.
Sea of Suph: the Red Sea.

Joshua charged the fathers to teach their children throughout the generations the miracle of the crossing of the river Jordan, just as they teach the miracle of the crossing of the Red Sea, when they see the twelve stones set up in Gilgal.

Because you are a human being and liable to forget, God calls you to remember His works with you, whether by thanking Him every day in your prayer or by writing down His works and His care for you in spiritual notebooks.
Joshua added that setting up the stones in Gilgal has two benefits:

1- When the nations surrounding the Jews see them, they feel the power of the God of the children of Israel, so they fear Him and do not harm His people, as they remember His power in the miracle of the crossing of the Jordan.
2- By the people of God remembering the miracle of the crossing of the Jordan, they fear the mighty God and so keep away from every sin and from the worship of idols.
We can arrange the events from the beginning of this book until now in the following order:
1- God commanded Joshua to prepare to depart to cross the Jordan on the third day of Nisan or a few days before that (ch. 1:1).
2- Joshua sent the two spies on the third day of Nisan, and they lodged that night in the house of Rahab (ch. 2:1).
3- The two spies hid three days in the mountain, which were the days 4, 5 and 6 of Nisan (ch. 2:22).
4- The two spies returned to Joshua on the sixth day of Nisan (ch. 2:23).
5- The leaders of the people went through them to gather provision on the seventh day of Nisan and informed them that they would cross the Jordan after three days (ch. 1:10, 11).
6- They journeyed from Shittim to the river Jordan on the ninth day of Nisan and lodged there (ch. 3:1).
7- They crossed the river Jordan on the tenth day of Nisan (ch. 4:19). Spiritual preparation for war
The Amorites: Canaanite tribes, some of them east of the Jordan and some west of it.
The sea: the Mediterranean Sea.
Melted: their souls grew very weak because of their fear.
Because of: on account of.

The Book of Deuteronomy. The kings of the Amorites west of the Jordan as far as the Mediterranean Sea heard of Joshua's defeat of Sihon king of the Amorites and Og king of Bashan east of the Jordan, and also of the Lord's drying up of the river Jordan before the people, and they were very afraid. And they remembered what happened to Pharaoh king of Egypt when he pursued the people after their departure and was drowned in the Red Sea, and so their fear increased. He mentioned the Amorites because they were the strongest of the Canaanite peoples dwelling in this region.
Flint: granite stone.

The children of Israel neglected circumcision in the wilderness of Sinai for 40 years, and the circumcised men who came out of Egypt had died in the wilderness. Therefore God admonished Joshua to make knives of hard flint stone to circumcise the males. Circumcision signifies Baptism, because in it a part of the flesh is cut off, which points to the nature inclined to evil, and the beginning of a new nature obedient to God. And because the sacrament of Baptism is the entrance to life in the Church, they performed circumcision before the war and the possession of the new land.
Foreskins: plural of foreskin, which is the extra skin that is cut off in circumcision.

The foreskins, a symbol of excessive, harmful desires, were removed and heaped upon one another; therefore they called this place "the hill of the foreskins", since the foreskins became a heap and they covered them with earth. In this way the circumcision of the people was accomplished as God commanded, and most likely those who circumcised the people were the priests and the Levites.
The men who came out of Egypt and were of the age for war had all been circumcised, but they died during the journey in the wilderness.
The wilderness: the wilderness of Sinai.

Flowing with milk and honey: it means the abundance of pastures in the new land, which makes the cattle give overflowing milk, and the abundance of crops and plants, which makes the bees' production of honey plentiful.

The men who came out of Egypt were circumcised, but they disobeyed God in the wilderness and refused to enter the Promised Land, so God swore that they would not enter the new land, full of good things, and they died in the wilderness. As for those born in the wilderness, they were not circumcised.
The Lord raised up the sons in the place of their fathers to fulfill His promise to them, and Joshua circumcised them as a sign of the renewal of the covenant with God.

They abode in their places until they were whole. This shows that a person's acceptance of the covenant with God is a joyful matter, but it calls for painful sufferings in striving, and the person must be patient and not move away from his covenant until God gives him victory over sin and healing from it (Lk 21:19), for "in your patience possess ye your souls". We notice that the fear of the peoples of the land of the Jews made them not attack them during the period of their pain after circumcision, as the sons of Jacob did to the people of Hamor and Shechem (Gen 34:25).

Sin is a burden that God rolls away, that is, takes down from our shoulders. The reproach of Egypt was the bondage of the Jews when they were in it, and then the mockery of the Egyptians toward them when they learned of their wandering in the wilderness for forty years without reaching the Promised Land. The place took its name from what happened in it.
How many of God's promises have we turned back from and not stood firm in, until God helps us by patience, prayer and striving, instead of our turning back and being defeated.
The Book of Deuteronomy

entries.section: (2) The Passover and the ceasing of the manna

paragraphs.text: The plains of Jericho: the flat lands of Jericho.

After the circumcision of the people, it became permissible for them, according to the Law, to eat the Passover, because no stranger or uncircumcised person is allowed to eat of it (Ex 12:44-49). If circumcision signifies Baptism, as does the crossing of the river Jordan, then the Passover signifies partaking of the Body and Blood of the Lord, and Communion is not permitted except to one who has been baptized.

It is noticed that this is the third time the children of Israel ate the Passover: the first time was at their departure from the land of Egypt (Ex 12), and the second in the second year of their departure (Num 9:1-5). The Passover was supposed to be kept every year, but it was not kept except when they entered the Promised Land.

entries.section: (2) The Passover and the ceasing of the manna

paragraphs.text: Old corn: fruits.
Parched corn: it is the wheat crop that is not fully ripe in the first of its season.

The people ate of the fruits of the Promised Land on the second day of the feast of the Passover, that is, the first of the week of unleavened bread, whether they had bought fruits from the merchants or found them as spoil in the houses of some Canaanites who fled for fear of the people. So they made unleavened cakes from the produce and fruits of the new land, and they ate unleavened bread because the Law prescribes eating unleavened bread for seven days after the feast of the Passover (Ex 12:15).

entries.section: (2) The Passover and the ceasing of the manna

paragraphs.text: When the children of Israel began to get food from the Promised Land, there was no longer a need for the manna, and God cut it off, because a person ought to work with his hands and toil to obtain his need; but if he meets circumstances harder than his abilities, such as the barren wilderness of Sinai, God will intervene, even by a miracle like the miracle of the manna.

Be faithful in bearing your responsibility and in using all your abilities for the glory of God. God rejoices in your striving and will hold you accountable for your neglect in everything in your hands. And be reassured about the future, because if any afflictions meet you, God will intervene and solve them for you.

entries.section: (3) Joshua and the captain of the host of the Lord

paragraphs.text: Drawn: out of its sheath.

Joshua was occupied with the coming war with Jericho, especially since it was a fortified city; if it defeated him, his reputation in the land would be lost and his defeat afterward would be made easy, and he could not pass it by and fight inside the land for fear of falling into an ambush with the city behind his back. Nor could he retreat, since he and the people had crossed the Jordan and it had become a barrier behind them.

At that time God intervened and sent the chief of His angels, or appeared Himself, as some Fathers see it. God in His love appears to His children in the form that suits them: He appeared to Abraham in the form of three strange men who passed by his tent in the wilderness, and to Jacob in the form of an angel wrestling with him and another time in the form of a multitude of angels to encourage him; and here, because Joshua was about to enter war, He appears to him in the form of a man of war holding a sword.
The Book of Deuteronomy. The faith and courage of Joshua appear in his going toward the man holding the sword and his asking him whether he was with us or against us.

entries.section: (3) Joshua and the captain of the host of the Lord

paragraphs.text: The man who appeared in the vision declared that he was the captain of the host of the Lord. The host of the Lord means the angels or the human believers in God, and what is meant by the captain of the host of the Lord is God Himself, because He accepted that Joshua worship Him, and He is also called the Lord Jehovah in. This worship is the worship of adoration and not merely respect.

entries.section: (3) Joshua and the captain of the host of the Lord

paragraphs.text: Shoe: sandal.
The Lord repeated in Joshua's hearing what He had said before to Moses at the bush (Ex 3:5), to teach him:
1- That the presence of the holy Lord had sanctified the whole place, for he was in the presence of the holy God.

2- That Joshua is not the bridegroom of the Church or her kinsman, but her friend [see the law of the loosing of the shoe (Deut 25:9).] For Christ is the only Kinsman or Savior of His Church, and Joshua and all the prophets or priests who serve in both Testaments are instruments in the hand of God and not the Kinsman; therefore they take off their sandals when approaching holy places.
3- That he might know that holiness, which is indicated by taking off the sandal made from the skin of a dead animal, is a life without which we shall not see the Lord (Heb 12:14).

God appears in your life, not only by visions but through the events of life, to encourage you, and you can feel Him if you seek Him from your heart, believe in His existence and are ready to obey Him; then He will make Himself known to you and guide you to live with Him.
The fall of Jericho

Jericho: city of the moon, that is, the moon god, and the meaning of the name is also sweet fragrances, because of the spread of roses and sweet basil in its land; it is located 8 km west of the river Jordan and 30 km east of Jerusalem (Map 1). It is the town of Zacchaeus the tax collector and of blind Bartimaeus in the New Testament. Straitly shut up: tightly shut.
Closed: tightly locked.

Jericho was the first city that the people faced in the Promised Land, and when its people saw the children of Israel in their tents opposite their city, after they had crossed the river Jordan, they shut the gates of their city tightly. The walls of Jericho were high and fortified, and perhaps watchmen were observing the movements of the children of Israel. All this shows how great the fear of the people of Jericho was of the children of Israel.

The Lord continues His speech with Joshua, affirming that they will take the city, and He uses the past tense to assure him of that victory over the city and all who are in it, however great their strength and might and however great the fortification of the city.

The Lord commanded the children of Israel to go around the city once each day for six days. The going around was of course at a sufficient distance for the circle to be wide, so as to include the very numerous people of the children of Israel, and so that they would be out of range of the arrows of the soldiers of Jericho on the walls. The people's going around the city has many benefits, the most important of which are:
1- God's encouragement of the people and instilling a spirit of confidence and strength in their hearts to storm Jericho.
2- Testing the people's obedience to God's commands so that they might obtain victory.

3- Instilling a spirit of fear in the inhabitants of Jericho who see the children of Israel from the walls, and through their fear their defeat is made easy, and fear may lead some of them to repentance and belief in God.
4- Teaching the children of Israel order and exactness in wars and in all their life.

The circle signifies eternity, so their going around Jericho signifies the necessity of thinking about and preparing for eternity so that a person may possess the Promised Land, which signifies the Kingdom of Heaven.

May you be obedient to God's commandments even if they seem to differ from your logic, and be confident that they are higher than your mind. Victory over Satan is by taking refuge in God and not by a person's confronting him relying on his own strength; as long as you hold fast to God, the power of Satan will collapse before you.
Trumpets: made from rams' horns and used in religious celebrations, giving out a strong sound that all the people hear.
The shout: a prolonged sound issuing from the trumpet, a strong sound announcing victory.

The ark of the covenant of God goes around in the procession around Jericho, preceded by seven priests with trumpets of shouting, which they blow on the seventh day after going around the city seven times, to proclaim the power of God and His victory over the wicked inhabitants of Jericho. Of course a number of priests, most likely four, were carrying the ark. The going around of the ark proclaims the presence of God in the midst of His people, who will give them victory over the enemies.

The people's going around for seven successive days implies that they went around on the Sabbath day as well. This is not a breaking of the Lord's commandment to sanctify the Sabbath day, because religious work or service is done on the Sabbath day, and it is not as the elders of the Jews thought, that no work is done on the Sabbath day, so that they opposed Christ for His healing of the sick (Mt 12:8). On the seventh day they go around seven times, and by this their strength is worn out, and then they blow the trumpets of shouting and shout, that is, it is God's power that will give them victory, and not their material strength or their weapons.

The going around for seven days, or seven times on the seventh day, signifies the work of the Holy Spirit in the seven sacraments in the Church, that is, that the people are subject to the Spirit of God, who will give them victory over the enemies.

God announced to them that after their going around Jericho seven times on the seventh day, and the priests' blowing of the trumpets of shouting and then the shout of all the people, the great walls of Jericho would fall, and then He commands them that every soldier is to rush upon the city wall that has collapsed before him, cross it and enter the city; that is, the circle of soldiers surrounding the city closes in on the city and storms it, killing those in it.

It is understood from this that the soldiers of war were in a circle around the city, and behind the soldiers within the circle was the ark of the covenant, with the priests carrying the trumpets before it; that is, the ark of the covenant was part of the circle, with the soldiers before it and behind it. The soldiers behind the ark He calls "the rereward", that is, the rear of the army.
Armed: the soldier prepared for war.
The rereward: the rear of the army.

Joshua carried out all that the Lord commanded, and the soldiers walked in a circle around the city, with the ark behind them and the bearers of the trumpets before it, and the rear of the army behind the ark; that is, the ark and the priests were between the soldiers before it and behind it. They blew the trumpet in intermittent blasts that frightened the enemies and encouraged the people of God. This is different from the continuous, strong blowing of the shouting which they did at the end of the going around on the seventh day.

Joshua commanded the people to walk in the procession around Jericho in silence, with nothing heard but the intermittent sound of the trumpets, and by this the people's obedience appears, their faith is strengthened, and they frighten their enemies, as we mentioned.

If we, the children of the Church, obey her teachings, our faith is strengthened and we frighten the demons; and by this we await God's victory. And as the people of God stormed Jericho, so also we triumph over Satan and set out for the Kingdom.

Joshua carried out God's commands and the procession went around the city, made up of the ark of the covenant carried by the priests, with the trumpeting priests before it and the soldiers before it and behind it; then they rested, and they did so on the second and third day until the sixth.
This procession was strange to the inhabitants of Jericho and the inhabitants of the neighboring lands, so some marveled, others mocked, and the rest were afraid.
It is noticed that Joshua rose early, as an active leader who carries out God's commands and leads his people with zeal.

entries.section: (2) The fall of the city and its being devoted to destruction

paragraphs.text: All the people rose early on the seventh day to go around the city of Jericho seven times, and perhaps they walked faster so that there would be time for the seven circuits.

entries.section: (2) The fall of the city and its being devoted to destruction

paragraphs.text: After going around seven times on the seventh day, the priests blew the trumpets with a continuous, strong blast, and Joshua commanded the people to shout the shout of victory because God had given them the city of Jericho, although their seizure of the city had not yet taken place, but Joshua speaks in the past tense because of his faith in the promises of God. The sound of the trumpets and the shout of the people stirred great fear in the hearts of the inhabitants of Jericho.

entries.section: (2) The fall of the city and its being devoted to destruction

paragraphs.text: Accursed to the Lord: devoted to Him, and it is not permissible for anyone to take any of it for himself.
Trouble it: bring evil upon it.

Joshua continued his speech with the people and commanded them not to take anything for themselves from the possessions of Jericho, but that everything be devoted to God and that people and animals be killed, except Rahab and her household, because she believed in God and hid the two spies whom Joshua sent to Jericho (ch. 2). He warned them that none of them should take possessions from Jericho, lest he be punished by God and bring evil upon all the people.

God intended the killing of the inhabitants of Jericho because of their evils, and likewise the animals and all the beasts because they were used as sacrifices to the idols or some of them were worshipped; that is, God wanted to remove evil and everything connected with it, and to make His people exact in keeping away from everything connected with evil. When the idea was established in their hearts, He afterward permitted them, in some of their wars, to take the spoils, as in their war with Ai (ch. 8).

entries.section: (2) The fall of the city and its being devoted to destruction

paragraphs.text: As for the metals of silver, gold, bronze and iron, they are holy to the Lord and are to be added to the treasury of the Tabernacle as the possessions of God.

entries.section: (2) The fall of the city and its being devoted to destruction

paragraphs.text: The Lord fulfilled His promise of the falling of the wall when they shouted, and they took the city and carried out the Lord's command to devote its people and all its spoil. Here appears the effectiveness of the faith that made the people obey God in going around Jericho and not murmur like their fathers, so the walls fell by the hand of God and not by the hand of man, and every Jewish soldier rushed straight before him, that is, the soldiers stormed the city from every side and killed those in it, and the inhabitants of Jericho surrendered because of their great fear.

By faith you can obtain all your needs from God according to His will. So remember God's works and promises so that your faith is strengthened, and ask Him with confidence and obey His commandments, and you will live in joy.

The two spies entered the house of Rahab at Joshua's command and brought her out with all her household, but they did not join them to the people; rather they left them outside the camp until they were cleansed of their uncleanness.
It is noticed that the house of Rahab, which was in the wall of the city, did not fall and collapse, by the Lord's command, in order to save her; for God is able to save everyone who believes in Him.

Rahab was a cause of blessing for her whole household and clan, for she announced to them deliverance if they believed, and they obeyed her and believed like her, and she saved them from death and they lived with the people of God, and God rewarded her by her becoming the grandmother of David and of Christ (Mt 1:5). By this the first Gentile pagan woman from the land of Canaan, she and all her household, was joined to the people of God, and many joined afterward.
Even unto this day: until the day Joshua wrote this book.

The silver and gold were added to the treasury of the Tabernacle, and Rahab and all her household were saved and joined the Jewish people as a reward for her kindness to the two spies. We see from the genealogy of Christ (Mt 1:5) that Salmon son of Nahshon, the prince of the tribe of Judah, married her.

Do not grow weary in doing good, for Rahab did a kindness to the two spies, and the course of her whole life changed and she joined the faith and the holy people. Be confident that a cup of cold water will not lose its reward (Mt 10:42).

Joshua regarded Jericho as an accursed city because of its immersion in evils and idol worship, therefore the Lord cursed it and devoted it to destruction and ruin. And Joshua decreed that the curse would come upon whoever builds this city again, since he would be opposing God, who demolished it and overthrew its walls Himself. In fulfillment of the curse, whoever dares to do so, his children will all die: his firstborn will die when he lays its foundation, then their deaths will follow one after another until the youngest of them dies when he sets up its gates. This was fulfilled five hundred years later in the person of Hiel the Bethelite (1 Kgs 16:34). It is noticed that the talk here is about building Jericho as a fortified city, which God commanded to be demolished, but buildings were afterward erected beside the ruined Jericho and called by its name, and it is in these that Elijah and Elisha established a school for the sons of the prophets, and Elisha healed its main spring of water (2 Kgs 2). Christ Himself visited Jericho and healed the two blind men near it and visited the house of Zacchaeus in it (Mt 9:27, Lk 19).
The report of God's work with Joshua and His support of him spread through all the land of Canaan. Defeat before Ai
In the accursed thing: in the forbidden things.
Achan: a name meaning troubling or disturbing.

Achan sinned against God by taking from the spoils of Jericho, from which God had commanded that no one should take, but that they be set apart for the house of the Lord. By his sin he stirred up the wrath of God against all the people, because Achan is a member of one body, so by his sin all the people sinned. In addition, the people were preoccupied with the victory and so were negligent in discovering Achan's theft of the spoils.

Ai: its meaning is a heap of stones, and it is a small city compared with Jericho, located east of Bethel (Map 2). Before attacking Ai, and without seeking the mind of God, Joshua sent men to discover its condition and fortifications, and they did as he asked. After Jericho Joshua began preparing to attack Ai because it was an entrance to the land of Canaan.
Mount Ebal
Mount Gerizim Bethel Gezer Ai Jarmuth Jerusalem Azekah Map (2)
The opinion of the spies when they returned to Joshua was that the city did not deserve the attack of all the people because of its smallness, but that two or three thousand men would suffice.
Shebarim: its meaning is stones, and it is located west of Ai; it is a slope between Ai and Jericho.
The heart of the people melted and became as water: they fell into great fear and weakness.

Joshua obeyed their advice, again without asking God His opinion, and the result was defeat and the death of thirty-six men of the people, and they pursued them down the slope on which the city was built, so the people were very afraid and terrified.
Be careful to take refuge in God in every great and small matter of your life, so that you learn humility and are reassured and protect yourself from every deviation.

Joshua and the leaders and elders of the people hurried to God and fasted and prayed with many supplications from morning until evening, and they humbled themselves before Him in prostration, and tore their clothes as a sign of their great grief, and put dust on their heads in humility and contrition before God.
The Amorites: tribes from the descendants of Canaan.

Joshua reproached God, who had permitted their crossing and dried up the river Jordan for them, as if God by this had delivered them to the inhabitants of the land so that they might destroy His people; indeed, in the weakness of his faith, he wished they had not crossed the Jordan and that it would have sufficed them to dwell east of it with the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh.

Joshua was deeply affected because the defeat of the people and their flight before their enemies would be heard of throughout the land, so that the inhabitants of Canaan would take courage and rise against the people of God and fight them and destroy them, and this would dishonor the name of God, as if the Lord had not been able to defend His people and so they perished.
Here Joshua appears as a spiritual leader who seeks the glory of God and the safety of his people.

The Lord had compassion on Joshua and commanded him to rise, and revealed to him the secret of the people's defeat before Ai, which was their offense against God by breaking their previous covenant to obey God and respect His commandments engraved on the tablets of the covenant. Their fall progressed from the offense to the transgression of the covenant by taking of the accursed things, then theft, denial and hiding among their stuff.
Accursed: falling under the curse of God because of the accursed thing in their midst.

The sin of the people was the cause of their defeat and of their not standing before the enemies, since they had become accursed like them, and God would not be with them unless they repented and removed the sin from their midst.

God asked Joshua to command the people to sanctify themselves, by bathing and washing their clothes and offering repentance before God, that is, washing their hearts; and He declares to them that the cause of their defeat before Ai is the presence of sin in their midst, and the accursed thing, that is, the sin, must be removed so that they may stand before the enemies.
Tribe: a clan.
Families: households.
Households: the families that dwell in this house.
Man by man: that is, every man with his family.

He also asked him that they should all come forward the next day to the tent of meeting, and the Lord would single out the guilty tribe, then the family within the tribe, then the guilty house, then the individual who committed the offense. This was done by means of the Urim and Thummim in the tent of meeting, which are two stones that the high priest carried, by which God declared His approval or refusal of anything, and the exposure of the guilty one may have been done by lot.
The guilty one must receive his punishment, which is burning with fire, he and what he stole and all that he has, for his transgression of the covenant of the Lord and his defiling of all the people.

A person falls into evil, and then his fall progresses until he becomes a slave to it and bound to it, and perishes. Blessed is he who examines himself first by first and saves himself from falling by repentance.

Joshua rose early the next day as was his habit, for he was an active man who hurries to carry out God's commands, and he did what God asked of him, and God determined that the guilty one was Achan of the tribe of Judah, and this was most likely done by lot. All this while Achan's conscience was not moved to offer repentance of his own accord and regret for the offense that caused the defeat and the death of thirty-six men. For sin will be exposed, even after a while, however much we hide it.
Joshua began a careful investigation with Achan and did not hasten to condemn him, but gave him an order to declare what he had done and not to hide any of it.
The following is noticed in Joshua's words with Achan:
1- His concern that there should be a public trial so that no one would think that God had wronged him.
2- Joshua's fatherliness and gentleness toward Achan, for he does not accuse him of anything before he confesses, although God had shown that he was a sinner, and so he addresses him, "My son."
3- He declares to Achan that his confession is not only before Joshua but before God first; therefore he demanded of him, saying, "Give glory to God."
Achan admitted his offense in detail after God had exposed him and he was compelled to admit it.

Achan saw, then coveted, then took, then hid in the ground. Thus he progressed in the offense for the sake of a costly mantle, silver coins and a wedge of gold, which he held on to for himself, contrary to the Lord's command to burn everything except the metals that were to be delivered to the tent of meeting.
Joshua sent messengers to verify the confession, and they found the stolen things and brought them to him, and this was clear evidence of accusation proving Achan's crime.

Joshua took the stolen things with all of Achan's possessions and all those who had supported him in his offense and covered up for him, his sons and daughters, and brought them to the valley of Achor.

Here Joshua, the deliberate leader, issued his final judgment on Achan, who had troubled all the people and so deserved that the Lord should trouble him. He was stoned, killed and burned, as was done with the people of Jericho whose possessions he had taken, so that it became necessary to treat him as one of them.

God refused to have the gold and silver brought into His house like the rest of the spoils of Jericho, because these were stolen goods; they were connected with the sin of Achan, and God rejects everything connected with sin.
Unto this day: the day Joshua wrote this book.

The people made a great heap of stones over Achan so that it would remain as long as possible and remind them of the consequence of treachery. Here the anger of God turned away from His people, but Achan lost everything he had stolen, and all his material possessions, and his whole life.

To everything under the heavens there is a time, so do not seek to acquire it before that time as Achan did and lost everything, whereas if he had waited until the conquest of Ai he would have obtained all that he wanted of the spoils without any punishment. So do not be preoccupied with material things, because your God arranges them for you at the proper time.

Victory over Ai (1) A well-ordered plan (vv. 1-8:) 1 And the Lord said unto Joshua, Fear not, neither be thou dismayed: take all the people of war with thee, and arise, go up to Ai: see, I have given into thy hand the king of Ai, and his people, and his city, and his land: 2 And thou shalt do to Ai and her king as thou didst unto Jericho and her king: only the spoil thereof, and the cattle thereof, shall ye take for a prey unto yourselves: lay thee an ambush for the city behind it. 3 So Joshua arose, and all the people of war, to go up against Ai: and Joshua chose out thirty thousand mighty men of valour, and sent them away by night. 4 And he commanded them, saying, Behold, ye shall lie in wait against the city, even behind the city: go not very far from the city, but be ye all ready: 5 And I, and all the people that are with me, will approach unto the city: and it shall come to pass, when they come out against us, as at the first, that we will flee before them, 6 (For they will come out after us) till we have drawn them from the city; for they will say, They flee before us, as at the first: therefore we will flee before them. 7 Then ye shall rise up from the ambush, and seize upon the city: for the Lord your God will deliver it into your hand. 8 And it shall be, when ye have taken the city, that ye shall set the city on fire: according to the commandment of the Lord shall ye do. See, I have commanded you.

After the removal of the accursed thing, God reassured Joshua and asked him to take the whole army with him as he did when entering Jericho, and not to make light of the enemies as he made light of them in the first attack on Ai, and the Lord promised him victory over the city.

He commanded the going out of all the warriors, whose number was about six hundred thousand (Num 11:21), not that they should all fight, because he had chosen from them thirty thousand (v. 3) to fight Ai because of its smallness, but the going out of the whole army was for the following reasons:
1- To encourage their brethren who would attack Ai.
2- That they might see God's victory and so be encouraged in their fighting of the enemies in all the land of Canaan.
3- That they might share in taking the spoils of the city of Ai.
And God says to Joshua, "I have given ... the king of Ai, and his people", in the past tense, for since God has commanded, His word will surely come to pass.

God announced to Joshua that he would triumph over Ai and possess it and kill its king as he did to Jericho. And God allowed him to let the people take the spoils of Ai. And He set for him a plan for the war, which was to make an ambush of men of war who would hide behind the city; this is a stratagem of war known from ancient times, and it shows the necessity that Joshua do everything in his power to conquer the city under God's guidance and not be idle, relying on God's giving him victory.
Lie in wait: hide without the people of Ai seeing you.
Joshua chose, by God's command, thirty thousand strong men of war, and commanded them to make an ambush, that is, to hide behind Ai and near it, and to be ready for war.
There are two opinions about the details of these war plans:

1- The thirty thousand are those who fought Ai, and five thousand of them lie in wait behind the city from the previous night (v. 12), while the rest, who are twenty-five thousand, attack the city in the early morning with Joshua; and when Joshua commands the thirty thousand to make the ambush, he means that part of them will do this work.

2- The second opinion is that thirty thousand made an ambush behind Ai made up of two parts, five thousand of them beside the city and twenty-five thousand behind Bethel, which is the helper and supporter of Ai (v. 17). As for the rest of the men of war among the children of Israel, whose number was six hundred thousand, they attacked the city in the morning under the leadership of Joshua himself.

Joshua completes the explanation of the plan to the men of war: that they should attack Ai, and when the men of Ai come out to fight, the army of the children of Israel withdraws before them, as the children of Israel withdrew from the first attack, noting the difference that in the first case they were defeated, whereas in the second case they pretend to be defeated in order to draw the army of Ai out of their city.
The men of Ai will be deceived and pursue the army of the children of Israel withdrawing before them, and will think that they are defeating them for the second time.
After the men of Ai have come out of it to pursue the army of the children of Israel, the ambush hidden behind Ai moves, enters the city and possesses it.
After the ambush of the children of Israel possesses the city of Ai, they burn it with fire, and by this they will have destroyed the evil and the wicked who are in the city.
If the devil fights us with many tricks, let us be confident that God is able to defeat him and guide us how to triumph over him.
We need only to obey God's commandments and the teachings of the Church.

(2) Carrying out the war plan (vv. 9-17:) 9 Joshua therefore sent them forth: and they went to lie in ambush, and abode between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of Ai: but Joshua lodged that night among the people. 10 And Joshua rose up early in the morning, and numbered the people, and went up, he and the elders of Israel, before the people to Ai. 11 And all the people, even the people of war that were with him, went up, and drew nigh, and came before the city, and pitched on the north side of Ai: now there was a valley between them and Ai. 12 And he took about five thousand men, and set them to lie in ambush between Bethel and Ai, on the west side of the city. 13 And when they had set the people, even all the host that was on the north of the city, and their liers in wait on the west of the city, Joshua went that night into the midst of the valley. 14 And it came to pass, when the king of Ai saw it, that they hasted and rose up early, and the men of the city went out against Israel to battle, he and all his people, at a time appointed, before the plain; but he wist not that there were liers in ambush against him behind the city. 15 And Joshua and all Israel made as if they were beaten before them, and fled by the way of the wilderness. 16 And all the people that were in Ai were called together to pursue after them: and they pursued after Joshua, and were drawn away from the city. 17 And there was not a man left in Ai or Bethel, that went not out after Israel: and they left the city open, and pursued after Israel.

The city of Ai was located southeast of Bethel, with rocky heights behind it, so the ambush of the children of Israel went by night and hid behind these heights west of Ai as Joshua had commanded them, while Joshua remained with the people and lodged among them that night (Map 2).
They had set: he means Joshua and the commanders of the army.

After Joshua sent the ambush at the beginning of the night to lie in wait west of Ai, he rose early before the dawn, that is, at the end of the night, and numbered his soldiers and moved with them toward Ai, which was located on a hill and could detect any military movements heading toward it in the daytime, and he reached the north of Ai with a valley separating him from it, while the ambush was hidden west of Ai between it and Bethel to attack Ai when Joshua commanded them. Then Joshua moved into the valley separating his forces from the city of Ai to inspect the place, and perhaps he withdrew to pray, asking God's help before the dawn and the attack on Ai.

At a time appointed: the suitable time that the king of Ai set, and most likely it is the time at which he had defeated the children of Israel the previous time. It may also be the time that Joshua set for carrying out his plan, and this shows the providence of God, who caused the king of Ai to come out to be defeated at the hands of the children of Israel.

At daybreak the king of Ai saw the armies of the children of Israel had come to attack him for the second time, so he gathered his army and went out with pride, confident of his victory over them as in the first time, and because of his pride he did not think that there might be an ambush against his city.
Made as if they were beaten: they pretended fear and flight.
Were called together: the king of Ai commanded his men to pursue the children of Israel.
They left the city open: that is, without guard, and therefore it is easy for the ambush to attack it.

The army of the children of Israel, under the leadership of Joshua, pretended fear of the army of Ai and fled before them by the way of the wilderness, and then the king of Ai commanded his armies to pursue the army of the children of Israel, so all the soldiers of Ai went out with pride, pursuing the children of Israel. The army of Bethel, which hurried to help the army of Ai, joined them, and all of them pursued the army of the children of Israel and left the city of Ai open and unguarded.

Pride made the king of Ai pursue the children of Israel and not guard against the possibility of an ambush. So be always humble, and God will reveal to you the devil's tricks and you will be able to overcome him. Be humble in your prayer before God and humble also in all your dealings with others, and you will secure your peace and your victory over Satan.

(3) The victory over Ai (vv. 18-29:) 18 And the Lord said unto Joshua, Stretch out the spear that is in thy hand toward Ai; for I will give it into thine hand. And Joshua stretched out the spear that he had in his hand toward the city. 19 And the ambush arose quickly out of their place, and they ran as soon as he had stretched out his hand: and they entered into the city, and took it, and hasted and set the city on fire. 20 And when the men of Ai looked behind them, they saw, and, behold, the smoke of the city ascended up to heaven, and they had no power to flee this way or that way: and the people that fled to the wilderness turned back upon the pursuers. 21 And when Joshua and all Israel saw that the ambush had taken the city, and that the smoke of the city ascended, then they turned again, and slew the men of Ai. 22 And the other issued out of the city against them; so they were in the midst of Israel, some on this side, and some on that side: and they smote them, so that they let none of them remain or escape. 23 And the king of Ai they took alive, and brought him to Joshua. 24 And it came to pass, when Israel had made an end of slaying all the inhabitants of Ai in the field, in the wilderness wherein they chased them, and when they were all fallen on the edge of the sword, until they were consumed, that all the Israelites returned unto Ai, and smote it with the edge of the sword. 25 And so it was, that all that fell that day, both of men and women, were twelve thousand, even all the men of Ai. 26 For Joshua drew not his hand back, wherewith he stretched out the spear, until he had utterly destroyed all the inhabitants of Ai. 27 Only the cattle and the spoil of that city Israel took for a prey unto themselves, according unto the word of the Lord which he commanded Joshua. 28 And Joshua burnt Ai, and made it an heap for ever, even a desolation unto this day. 29 And the king of Ai he hanged on a tree until eventide: and as soon as the sun was down, Joshua commanded that they should take his carcase down from the tree, and cast it at the entering of the gate of the city, and raise thereon a great heap of stones, that remaineth unto this day.
Spear: a lance.

God is the commander of the army of His people in war, for after all the soldiers of Ai and Bethel had gone out, God commanded Joshua to raise the spear toward Ai, and the soldiers hidden in the ambush saw it, and then they hurried and seized the city of Ai and burned it, and the flames rose to heaven, so as to frighten the soldiers of Ai and make it easy to defeat them.
Turned again: returned.
Remain or escape: a fugitive.

The soldiers of Ai were surprised by smoke filling the air, and they turned behind them to find their city burning, and they were alarmed and bewildered, and while they were alarmed, the soldiers of the children of Israel who were pretending to flee before the soldiers of Ai turned around and attacked the soldiers of Ai, and the soldiers of the ambush also attacked the soldiers of Ai and the soldiers of Bethel, so that they were surrounded between the soldiers of the children of Israel, and they killed them all and none escaped.

Since the soldiers of Ai were alarmed, it became easy for the soldiers of the children of Israel to seize their king and hand him over to Joshua, and this increased their alarm and despair, which helped the soldiers of Israel to kill the soldiers of Ai. Then they entered the city of Ai and killed all who were in it, women, old people and children, as the Lord commanded, to remove evil.

The number of persons killed in Ai was twelve thousand, and the dead of Bethel were not mentioned because the emphasis was on the victory over Ai. Joshua may have taken Bethel at this time or afterward, but in any case he took it among the cities in Canaan (ch. 12:16). Joshua kept the spear raised throughout the battle, as Moses raised his hands like a cross in the victory over Amalek (Ex 17), and this was by God's command so that the eyes of the warriors would remain on the spear, which signifies the cross, and they would be united together and so achieve a complete victory.

The children of Israel took the spoil of the city for themselves, according to God's word to Joshua, and had Achan waited he would have taken many things and not lost his life and possessions (ch. 7).

Joshua completed the burning of all of Ai, and it became a heap of rubble and was turned from a city of importance into a mound, and by this he removed the evil and uncleanness that had filled the place.

They hanged the king of Ai on a tree, which was a means of killing the worst offenders and an example of shame and disgrace, and at evening they took his body down as the Law prescribes (Deut 21:23) and cast it at the gate of the city and raised over it a heap of stones, so that everyone who sees the heap or the mound of the city knows the end of evil and the wicked.
