If God is the leader of your life, be confident that you are able to triumph in all the wars of the demons; He will guide you and support you, and do not be alarmed at all their movements and tricks, because your God is with you. Hold fast to Him and seek Him, and He will always lead your life.

(4) The blessing and the curse (vv. 30-35:) 30 Then Joshua built an altar unto the Lord God of Israel in mount Ebal, 31 As Moses the servant of the Lord commanded the children of Israel, as it is written in the book of the law of Moses, an altar of whole stones, over which no man hath lift up any iron: and they offered thereon burnt offerings unto the Lord, and sacrificed peace offerings. 32 And he wrote there upon the stones a copy of the law of Moses, which he wrote in the presence of the children of Israel. 33 And all Israel, and their elders, and officers, and their judges, stood on this side the ark and on that side before the priests the Levites, which bare the ark of the covenant of the Lord, as well the stranger, as he that was born among them; half of them over against mount Gerizim, and half of them over against mount Ebal; as Moses the servant of the Lord had commanded before, that they should bless the people of Israel. 34 And afterward he read all the words of the law, the blessings and cursings, according to all that is written in the book of the law. 35 There was not a word of all that Moses commanded, which Joshua read not before all the congregation of Israel, with the women, and the little ones, and the strangers that were conversant among them.

Mount Ebal: a mountain located north of Shechem (present-day Nablus), on which six tribes stood to proclaim the curse of those who violate the Law and the divine commandments (Map 2). Whole stones: sound stones with even faces, prepared.

After that victory Joshua built an altar on Mount Ebal according to the conditions Moses had taught him (Deut 27:5), that the altar be built of sound stones and that no chisel be lifted upon it while they were building it, out of care not to resemble the altars of idols on which their images and statues were engraved. They offered to the Lord burnt offerings and peace offerings of thanksgiving, and he built the altar on Mount Ebal, on which the divine curses were recited upon whoever disobeys God (Deut 27:11-26), to confirm the uprightness of the people of God and their keeping away from these curses and their obedience to His commands, which led to their victory over Ai.
They set up pillars of stone and coated them with lime or some similar material to make it easy to write on them, and then they wrote on them the commandments and the Law.
Officers: leaders of the people who understand the Law, and they are deputies of the elders.

Moses had commanded his people that if they entered the Promised Land they should set up an altar to the Lord and offer thank offerings and write a copy of the Law on stone pillars for the people to read and remember, and proclaim the blessings of God upon whoever obeys Him and His curses upon whoever disobeys Him, on Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal (Deut 27:11-26). So Joshua carried out all that Moses commanded, and the priests bore the ark, and the elders of the people and their officers and judges stood around the ark on the right and on the left, and with them the people, who were in two parts, six tribes at Mount Gerizim and six tribes at Mount Ebal, and all the Jews stood, both the native-born and the strangers who joined them and became Jews, because God is the God of the whole world, who desires the salvation of all through faith.

After the proclamation of the blessing and the curse and the ratification of them by both parties, Joshua completed the reading of the commandments of the Lord and the Law which He had delivered to Moses, before all the people, and explained it (Deut 31:12).

May you read the Holy Bible every day, and also repeat some of its verses that you choose, to keep your mind and heart pure throughout your day and so that you do not turn aside from them into any sin, and you will receive the abundant blessings of God in your life. The trick of the Gibeonites
Beyond Jordan: what is meant is the west bank of the river Jordan.
The great sea: the Mediterranean Sea.
The Hittites, the Amorites, the Canaanites and the Perizzites: Canaanite tribes.

After the victory over Jericho and Ai, a general tension arose among the kings of the main cities lying west of the river Jordan as far as the coast of the Mediterranean Sea, in all the regions, mountains and plains alike.
The kings of the lands lying west of the Jordan agreed to unite together and fight the children of Israel so that it would be easy to defeat them.

Do not be troubled if the wicked agree against you, however strong or numerous they appear, for they are nothing before the power of God that is with us. Present your need before God and make supplication to Him, and you will stand firm and no one will be able to overcome you.

Gibeon: its meaning is a hill, and it is a city located nine kilometers north of Jerusalem and strongly fortified (Map 1). The Lord had designated for His people seven tribes with whom they were not to make a covenant but to devote them to destruction because of their many evils (Deut 7:

1-2) They are the Hittites, the Girgashites, the Amorites, the Canaanites, the Perizzites, the Hivites and the Jebusites, and the inhabitants of Gibeon were of the Hivites, and they had heard of the victory of the Jews over Jericho and Ai and the killing of their inhabitants, so they were very afraid and devised a plan to escape from the hands of the children of Israel.
Wilily: deceit.
Sacks: bags and sacks.
Bottles: leather vessels for carrying water or wine.
Old: ancient and tattered.
Crumbs: small pieces.

The Gibeonites deceived the Jews, pretending that they had come from a far country, and they took old sacks and put in them dry, crumbled bread and old wineskins full of holes, and they bound up the holes so that they were stopped, and put on old sandals and tattered clothes, and loaded their donkeys and came to the Jews.

The Jews were camped at Gilgal, which is near Jericho (ch. 4:19), and the Gibeonites asked them to make a peace treaty, and the Jews hesitated lest they be of the inhabitants of the nearby land that the Lord had promised them as an inheritance and whose people He had commanded to be devoted to destruction.

When Joshua asked them about their origin and where they dwelt, they lied to him, claiming that they had come from a far country, believing in the power and greatness of God when they heard of the ten plagues that the Lord brought on the Egyptians and the drowning of Pharaoh and his army in the sea.

They also heard of the victory of the Jews over the kings of the Amorites, Sihon and Og, east of the Jordan, and Og dwelt in his capital Ashtaroth. The lands of these two kings were east of the Jordan and were taken by the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh after they defeated these two kings and their armies (Deut 2, 3).

The Gibeonites said, "Our elders, when they heard the news of your power and your victories, told us to take provision with us and travel to you and ask you to make a covenant with us, and we will be your servants. And the proof that we dwell in a place very far from you is that our bread which we took as provision when we set out was hot, and now it has become not only dry but crumbs, and our wineskins, which were new, have burst from the length of the journey, and our sandals have worn out from much walking."

Be careful in your life, so that the devil does not deceive you with his tricks, and in order to discover them, examine whether the thought or matter presented to you brings you nearer to God, leads you to edification and gives you rest and peace, and make sure of that through prayer. If it is so, it is from God, and if it is the opposite, it is from Satan, however logical it appears, because the devil interprets reality with his evil thoughts to deceive you and take you away from God.

entries.section: (3) The Gibeonites as slaves to the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The Jews and Joshua took of the Gibeonites' food and ate with them, as a sign of peace and covenant not to harm, and they swore to them by the name of the Lord to confirm that. This was done without their praying to God and asking His opinion, exactly as they did when they fought Ai without taking God's opinion, and they were defeated.

entries.section: (3) The Gibeonites as slaves to the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: After the covenant was made, the Gibeonites returned to their country, and after three days the children of Israel discovered that they lived near them, and perhaps they learned this from some merchants, or some of the neighboring Canaanite inhabitants informed on them because they were angry with them for their covenant with the children of Israel.

entries.section: (3) The Gibeonites as slaves to the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The children of Israel journeyed on the road to the country of the Gibeonites and reached it after three days, which means that it is about 39 kilometers from them, and they could not fight their four cities mentioned, because they had made a covenant with them. And the people murmured against Joshua and against the leaders for making this covenant, either because some of them held fast to God and were distressed at the lack of prayer and of taking His opinion before the covenant, or because others wanted to take the spoils of these lands after fighting them and defeating them.

entries.section: (3) The Gibeonites as slaves to the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The leaders declared that there could be no turning back after the oath, as it says in (Ps 15:4) that whoever knows God swears to his own hurt and changes not, that is, does not go back on his oath even if he suffers harm or loss, otherwise harm would come on them from the Lord. And we shall see afterward in (2 Sam 21:1, 2) that when Saul dealt treacherously with the Gibeonites and killed them, there was wrath from God against him, and accordingly the leaders told them that it was not possible to fight them or kill them.

entries.section: (3) The Gibeonites as slaves to the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: The leaders sentenced them to work at gathering wood and drawing water for all the people and for the tent of meeting. And Joshua reproached them for deceiving him by claiming that their country was far away when it was near. By this the Gibeonites became slaves to the children of Israel, working at tasks that helped them.

entries.section: (3) The Gibeonites as slaves to the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: Joshua cursed them and declared to them his previous judgment, that is, that their curse is that they became slaves to the children of Israel, and they excused themselves that they were very afraid when they learned that the Lord had promised Moses and the people this land and the destruction of its inhabitants, so they did this trick to save themselves and their country from destruction, and they left their case to Joshua to do with them as he saw fit. This shows that they believed in the power of the God of the children of Israel, like Rahab.

entries.section: (3) The Gibeonites as slaves to the children of Israel

paragraphs.text: In the place which he should choose: the place of the house of the Lord, which is the tent of meeting or the temple of Solomon.

Joshua judged as he judged and did not allow the people to kill them, and they continued to carry out the sentence and served the people and the tent of meeting until the days of the writing of the book of Joshua, and their service to the temple continued after it was built.

Afterward they were called the Nethinim, that is, those dedicated to the service of God, since they were helpers to the Levites in gathering wood and carrying the water needed by the house of the Lord.

The Gibeonites believed in the power of God, so they received life and became servants of the house of God. And you, by faith, receive eternal life, and God favors you with serving Him and you enjoy fellowship with Him.
The victory over the five kings

entries.section: (1) The five kings' war against Gibeon

paragraphs.text: Adonizedec: a name meaning lord of righteousness.

Jerusalem: Ur means light, and Shalem means peace, so its meaning is light of peace, and it is commonly called the city of peace; it is present-day Jerusalem (al-Quds) and is located northwest of the Dead Sea at a distance of 14 miles. When Adonizedec king of the city of Jerusalem, the largest city in the group of five cities west of the Jordan, which lies beyond Gibeon and was exposed to Joshua's attack upon it, heard that Joshua had killed the people of Jericho and the people of Ai, and heard also of the peace of the Gibeonites with Joshua, which would weaken his position and that of his neighbors before Joshua, since Gibeon lies in the midst of their cities.

entries.section: (1) The five kings' war against Gibeon

paragraphs.text: The king of Jerusalem was afraid because the city of Gibeon was a great city like the cities ruled by kings and called royal cities, that is, great and principal, and all its men were mighty in war, but it feared the children of Israel and made peace with them.

entries.section: (1) The five kings' war against Gibeon

paragraphs.text: Hebron: present-day Hebron (al-Khalil), located 30 kilometers south of Jerusalem.
Jarmuth: a city about 25 kilometers west of Jerusalem.
Lachish: a fortified city located in the possession of the tribe of Judah.
Eglon: a city in the possession of the tribe of Judah, located 15 km northeast of Gaza (Map 3). The Amorites: the strongest of the Canaanite peoples.

Adonizedec moved to form an alliance of four kings with him from the nearby cities so that they might begin to fight Joshua before he surprised them with war. Their plan began with declaring war on Gibeon, the ally of Joshua, to draw him into war with them, and so five Amorite kings gathered to fight Gibeon. Gaza Map (3)

entries.section: (1) The five kings' war against Gibeon

paragraphs.text: The mountain: the mountains lying southwest of Jerusalem.
Mighty men of valour: strong men of war.

The Gibeonites cried out fervently to their ally Joshua to hurry to their help in repelling that attack of the five, so Joshua moved with his mighty army from Gilgal to their rescue and hastened toward Gibeon.

The five kings in their alliance were thinking of defeating Joshua, but God used their alliance to deliver them together as spoil to Joshua and give him victory over them. Your God is able to turn the plots of the wicked into a blessing for you and a cause of salvation and victory, for He turns evil into good.

entries.section: (2) Joshua's victory and the help of heaven for him

paragraphs.text: The Lord reassured Joshua that He had indeed delivered these five kings into his hand and that he would defeat them, and He said "I have delivered them" in the past tense, because since God has commanded, His word will surely come to pass.

entries.section: (2) Joshua's victory and the help of heaven for him

paragraphs.text: Suddenly: all at once.

Joshua exerted himself and marched all night from Gilgal to Gibeon, a distance of about 39 kilometers, to attack the five kings suddenly and so prevail over them. His moving during the night was something the enemies did not expect, and it shows faithfulness on his part and also skill in war.

entries.section: (2) Joshua's victory and the help of heaven for him

paragraphs.text: Azekah: a city located 18 kilometers west of Jerusalem.
The going up to Beth-horon: a projecting rock located 18 kilometers northwest of Jerusalem.

Makkedah: a city located south of Jerusalem (Map 3). God discomfited the five kings, and they were greatly afraid of the children of Israel, and it became easy for Joshua to strike them with a great slaughter and chase them from before Gibeon to the going up to Beth-horon, to Azekah and Makkedah.

entries.section: (2) Joshua's victory and the help of heaven for him

paragraphs.text: Hailstones: balls of ice reaching 15 cm in diameter that can break or kill any human they strike.
The Lord cast down upon them from heaven heavy hailstones, which killed more of them than those who died by the sword of the children of Israel.

entries.section: (2) Joshua's victory and the help of heaven for him

paragraphs.text: Ajalon: a city located at a distance of 21 kilometers west of Jerusalem.

While Joshua was fighting the five kings gathered before Gibeon and his victory over them had begun, the sun was about to set, so he asked God that the sun continue to shine so that he might complete his victory over the kings, and he commanded the sun to remain shining over Gibeon and the moon over the valley of Ajalon, which is a city located beside Gibeon. People sometimes see the sun and the moon at the same time at sunset, and this shows the authority of the children of God over nature.

entries.section: (2) Joshua's victory and the help of heaven for him

paragraphs.text: The book of Jasher: a book in poetry and prose that records the important events in the history of the Jews.
The midst of heaven: the height and middle of the sky.

God answered, and Gibeon continued to be lit until Joshua overcame the enemies ... and this event was recorded in the book of Jasher. Thus the day was prolonged until Joshua completed his victory over the kings, and this wonderful answer of God was one of the greatest miracles and a proof that God fights with Joshua and his people. This means that God the Almighty stopped the whole universe for the sake of His son Joshua who made supplication to Him, and He stopped any side effects of the sun's remaining for a long period over the earth, so no harm occurred, and this stopping was for a whole day. Historians of that era have mentioned the existence of a long day, such as Herodotus the Greek, the writer of the history of Egypt, and also the historians of China.
God supports you as His son in ways you accept and ways you cannot imagine. Trust in Him with all your heart, keep His commandments, and do not fear the ferocity of the enemy.

entries.section: (3) The pursuit of the enemies and the killing of their kings

paragraphs.text: After the victory the people returned to Gilgal, but the five kings fled after the defeat of their armies and hid in a cave at Makkedah.

entries.section: (3) The pursuit of the enemies and the killing of their kings

paragraphs.text: The hindmost of them: the rear of the fleeing army.

When Joshua learned of this, he commanded the people to close the mouth of the cave upon them by placing great stones against it, and not to occupy themselves with them for now but to be content with confining them and guarding them lest they escape, while the people continued pursuing their enemies and smiting the rear of their armies in their flight to prevent them from returning to hide in their cities and renewing their strength to resume the war, because God had decreed their destruction.

entries.section: (3) The pursuit of the enemies and the killing of their kings

paragraphs.text: Those that remained: those who separated from the army and scattered to flee.
Move his tongue: speak with blame.

This continued until the great victory was achieved, and none of the enemies escaped except those who succeeded in fleeing and hiding in the fortified cities. And all the people returned victorious to Joshua at Gilgal, with none of the inhabitants of the land able to harm them.

entries.section: (3) The pursuit of the enemies and the killing of their kings

paragraphs.text: Then Joshua commanded that the cave be opened and the five kings brought out of their confinement, and they brought them out.

entries.section: (3) The pursuit of the enemies and the killing of their kings

paragraphs.text: They bound the five kings and cast them on the ground before Joshua, and Joshua called the commanders of the army to put their feet on the necks of those five kings as a sign of their victory over them, and they did so. And Joshua asked them not to fear in the future but to be encouraged by God, who will always give them victory over their enemies. Joshua did not mean by this gloating or rage and revenge against the kings, but he meant the following:
1- Proclaiming the authority of God and His crushing of all the wicked, however great they are, and showing the worthlessness of the power of their pagan gods.
2- Encouraging his army to tread down and triumph over all the peoples of Canaan.
3- Frightening and disturbing all the kings of Canaan who would hear this news.

entries.section: (3) The pursuit of the enemies and the killing of their kings

paragraphs.text: Joshua killed the five kings with the sword and hanged them on wooden trees until evening, and commanded that their bodies be taken down from the trees at sunset, being content with what had happened so as not to be excessive in punishment, as the Law prescribed (Deut 21:22, 23); and hanging on a tree had been a symbol of shame and disgrace from ancient times. Then they buried them in the cave in which they had hidden and closed it with stones, to the day of the writing of the book.

Do not hinder yourself from positive work by being occupied with negative things. Striving for spiritual progress and constructive work are more important and more lasting in benefit than being occupied with side matters that hinder a person.

entries.section: (4) The subjugation of the cities of the south

paragraphs.text: After Joshua finished subduing the central sector of the region west of the Jordan, he moved on his way to the southern sector, and took Makkedah and killed its king and devoted its people to destruction as he did to Jericho.

entries.section: (4) The subjugation of the cities of the south

paragraphs.text: Libnah: a city located 18 km southwest of Jerusalem.
Lachish: a city located south of Libnah.

Gezer: a city located 30 km west of Jerusalem (Map 3). Then he came to Libnah and did the same to it, then to Lachish to the south and besieged it two days, then Gezer, and did the same to both. Thus he killed all who were in these lands and their kings, and conquered and took possession of them.

entries.section: (4) The subjugation of the cities of the south

paragraphs.text: Eglon: a city located 15 km northeast of Gaza.

Hebron: present-day Hebron (al-Khalil), located 30 km south of Jerusalem (Map 3). Then he repeated the same action at Eglon and Hebron and the cities belonging to them, and they killed the new king of Hebron who had been set up after the king who was killed with the five kings (vv. 23, 26), and he killed all who were in these lands and took possession of them.

entries.section: (4) The subjugation of the cities of the south

paragraphs.text: Debir: a city near Hebron, which was the seat of religious learning among the Canaanites (Map 3). Then he returned to Debir and took it despite the greatness of its religious standing among the Canaanites, and did the same to it, killing its king and all who were in it and taking possession of it.

entries.section: (4) The subjugation of the cities of the south

paragraphs.text: All the country of the hills: the mountainous lands that were in the portion of the tribes of Judah and Ephraim. The south: the Negev, which is the south of the Promised Land.
The vale: the lowlands on the coast of the Mediterranean Sea.
The springs: the sloping lands lying at the foot of the mountains.

Thereby Joshua took possession of all the hill country lying in the portion of Judah and Ephraim, and the vale and the slopes of the mountains, and killed and devoted to destruction all their kings and their people, according to the Lord's command.

entries.section: (4) The subjugation of the cities of the south

paragraphs.text: At one time: that is, he did not stop the war and took possession of these lands in a short time by the power of God.
Kadesh-barnea: located on the southern border of Canaan.
Goshen: located in the possession of Judah, south of Hebron.

Joshua took possession of the lands lying from the border of the land of Canaan in the south to Gaza in the west and all the land of the region that Judah inhabited, and this was done at one time with God's help to Joshua and to the people, and then Joshua returned with all the people to Gilgal.
As Joshua achieved many victories by the miraculous power of God, be confident that God is able to work with you so that you triumph over all the wars of the devil, however strong he is.
Kings of the north, east and west of Canaan
Jabin: a title of the king of Hazor, who was the greatest of the Canaanite kings in position in the north.
Hazor: a city in northern Canaan.
Madon: a city in northern Canaan.
Shimron: a city in northern Canaan, located in the portion of Zebulun, 17 kilometers southeast of Nazareth.
Achshaph: a city in northern Canaan, located in the portion of Asher.
The Arabah: the plain (level land.) Chinneroth: the Lake of Gennesaret, or the Sea of Tiberias, or the Sea of Galilee.
The heights of Dor: a city on the shore of the Mediterranean Sea, 15 kilometers from Caesarea of Palestine (Map 4). The east and the west: what is meant is the east and west of the Jordan River.

The Amorites, the Hittites, the Perizzites, the Jebusites and the Hivites: Canaanite tribes [see (Gen 10:15-18, Josh 9:1.[)]. Hermon: a mountain located northeast of the Sea of Galilee (Map 4). Under Hermon: at the foot of Mount Hermon (today Mount Sheikh).

Mizpah: a city west of Hermon (today the Beqaa), located in the northeast of Palestine. After Joshua's victory over the five kings who lived in the south of Palestine (ch. 10), the chief of the kings of the Amorites in the north moved and sent to his neighbors, the kings of the principal cities east and west of the Jordan, to join together in confronting the coming Jewish danger.
Mount Hermon, Merom, Madon, Sea of Galilee, Joppa, Ashdod, Gath, Ashkelon, Hebron, Debir, Gaza, Goshen. Map (4)

The waters of Merom: Lake Huleh, which is on the course of the Jordan River and lies 17 kilometers north of Lake Tiberias (Map 4). They gathered very large armies with horsemen and war chariots, and assembled together at the waters of Merom to fight at one appointed time. Perhaps they chose this place because it lay midway between their lands and because of the abundance of its water.

The enemy strives to gather his devices and his soldiers to deliver a deadly blow, and God intervenes to make the destruction of the enemy gathered in one place, which is quicker than destroying every city by itself. Just as the enemy has his plans, God has His prevailing plans.
To hamstring: to cut the sinews, ligaments and blood vessels of a horse's leg so that it is unable to run and cannot be used in war.

The Lord gave Joshua assurance that He would defeat them after one day, so he must not fear. And He asked him to hamstring the horses and burn the chariots, so that the enemies would not use them in new wars in the future, and so that the people also would not use them and rely on them instead of God, as He had commanded them in (Deut 17:16). He set for them a time in which they would conquer the enemies, and this really happened, because the people trusted in God. As for the enemies, they set a time, but they trusted in themselves, so they were defeated.
Suddenly: all at once.
Joshua attacked them suddenly and fell upon them. Here appears the importance of faithfulness in the striving that God supports, so that it succeeds.

Zidon: the city of Sidon, between Beirut and Tyre, located on the Mediterranean Sea (Map 4). Misrephoth-maim: it means burnings of water, and it is a place with hot water springs, located 5 kilometers south of Sidon.
God delivered them into his hand, so he defeated them, drove them out of the land and destroyed their soldiers, and none of them was able to escape.
Joshua did to them what God had asked of him: he hamstrung the horses and burned the chariots.

Since God reassures us, let us drive out fear, because everything is in God's hand. Let us only obey His commandments faithfully and carefully, and not be troubled however difficult the surrounding circumstances may be, because God is stronger than everything.
He utterly destroyed them: he put them under the ban and killed them, as the Lord commanded, because of their terrible evils.

Joshua destroyed the king of Hazor, the leader of evil in the region, and put its people under the ban and burned it, as the Lord commanded. He took all the cities that he had defeated and put their people under the ban, as Moses his teacher had commanded him. But he left the cities that stood on their mounds, because they were naturally fortified and the Jews would benefit from them, so he did not destroy them. He burned only Hazor, in order to remove evil, to frighten the rest, and to show them their weakness, so that they would abandon their reliance on idols.
The people took the spoil of the cities and killed their men, as the Lord had commanded Moses. And Joshua carried out completely what Moses had commanded him, and neglected nothing of it.

Goshen: it lies in the portion of Judah, 21 kilometers south of Hebron (Al-Khalil) (Maps 4, 5). Mount Halak: a mountain bare of trees near Beersheba, 30 kilometers south of Hebron, and at it Joshua's wars in the south ended.
Seir: the land between the Dead Sea and the Gulf of Aqaba.
Baal-gad: the name of a city meaning the camp of Baal. It lies on the northern border of Joshua's wars, at the foot of Mount Hermon, and was afterwards called Caesarea Philippi, and today Banias.

By Joshua's victory over the kings of Canaan in the north, east and west of Palestine, he took possession of the Canaanite lands in the north and in the south, as is made clear by the places mentioned in these verses and explained above. The wars continued for about seven years, because Joshua was 40 years old when Moses sent him to spy out the land (Josh 14:7); then they wandered in the wilderness 38 years, after which he began to lead the people at the age of 78. And when he divided the land among the people (Josh 14:10) he was 85 years old.
The wars lasted a long time for the following reasons:
1- So that the prayers of God's people would increase, and their experience of His power working with them.
2- So that He might give the pagan peoples an opportunity to repent and believe in God.
3- So that God's people would not quickly grow weary from successive wars, which would be beyond their strength.
4- To train His people in patience and endurance.
5- Because if He had driven out the peoples quickly, His people would not have been able to fill their places, and wild beasts would have dwelt in them (Deut 7:22).

None made peace with the Jews without war except the Gibeonites, who were one of the tribes of the Hivites. As for the rest of the Canaanites, their hearts were hardened to evil and God left them to their hardness, until God's judgment of extermination was carried out on them. God is not cruel to them; rather He was long-suffering toward them for hundreds of years, and as a result of their many evils He commanded His people to exterminate them.

The Anakim: peoples who live south of Jerusalem as far as Hebron, which lies in the south of Palestine, west of the Dead Sea, and which was called Kirjath-arba. They are the giants whom Moses' spies saw and were afraid, and the Lord decreed their wandering 38 years in the wilderness.
At that time: after Joshua finished fighting the kings of the north and the south.
He cut off the Anakim: he destroyed them.
Anab: it lies 25 km south of Hebron, and vineyards were abundant in it.
Debir: the religious city of the Canaanites, located near Hebron.
Gaza: it exists today.
Ashdod: between Gaza and Joppa.

Gath: it lies 25 kilometers east of Ashdod. All the preceding cities are Philistine cities (Map 4). Joshua took the land of the Anakim who lived south of Jerusalem and in the mountains that the tribe of Judah took, which are part of the mountains in Canaan that the people of Israel took. So they fled and lived with the Philistines in their coastal cities, such as Gaza, Ashdod and Gath, which Joshua did not take. We shall see that Joshua divided the land among the tribes, and there were no more wars for a long time.

God gave His people to possess the Promised Land and to destroy the wicked in it. So He gives you many good things if you walk uprightly before Him, and you live in peace and inherit the Kingdom of Heaven. But if you neglect His commandments you will become troubled like the wicked, and you will have no place with Him in the Kingdom.
The borders of the Promised Land

entries.section: (1) The land east of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: The land east of the Jordan is the land that the Jews took by war under the leadership of Moses, and in which the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh settled. It extends from the valley of the Arnon River in the south, a small river among the tributaries of the Jordan River that flows into it. Its northern border is Mount Hermon (today Mount Sheikh), and it includes the whole Arabah, that is, the valley lying east of the Jordan. It includes the kingdoms of Sihon and Og, in addition to other kingdoms that the tribe of Manasseh took (Num 21, Deut 2:26-37, 3:1-17) (Map 5). Map (5)

entries.section: (1) The land east of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: The land east of Canaan was owned by Sihon king of the Amorites, an ancient people. Its capital was the city of Heshbon, which they had seized from the Moabites (the descendants of Lot.) He reigned over the land from north of the Arnon River, where the city of Aroer is, including the river itself in the middle of the Arnon valley, and the whole valley in which the Arnon River lies, to half of Mount Gilead, which extends east of the Jordan as far as the land of the Arabs and is now called Al-Balqa, and the valley of the Jabbok River on the border of the land of the children of Ammon. These lands were mentioned in (Num 21:25-30).

entries.section: (1) The land east of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: Teman: the south.

These lands also include the Arabah, that is, the plain extending to the Sea of Chinneroth (the Sea of Galilee) in the north, to the Salt Sea (the Dead Sea) in the south, and Beth-jeshimoth, a city northwest of the Dead Sea (Num 33:49). The southern border was Mount Pisgah, one of the mountains of Abarim east of Jericho, and from Pisgah Moses saw the Promised Land before he died (Num 21:20), (Deut 34:1).

entries.section: (1) The land east of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: Ashtaroth: it lies east of the Sea of Galilee.
Edrei: it lies southeast of the Sea of Galilee.

It passes along the border of the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, whom the Jews had defeated earlier, and they annexed his land to their country. This land had formerly belonged to the tribe of the Rephaim east of the Jordan, who lived in the cities of Ashtaroth and Edrei and made them their two capitals.

entries.section: (1) The land east of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: It included Mount Hermon (Mount Sheikh) and the city of Salcah, which lies on the eastern border of Bashan at the edge of the southern Druze mountain, and all the plain of Bashan east of the Jordan as far as the border of the kingdom of the Geshurites. Geshur lies south of Hermon, and the Maachathites in the northeast of Palestine beside Geshur (Deut 3:14) (Map 5). Half Gilead, the border of Sihon king of Heshbon: Sihon had taken the southern half of Mount Gilead, and his capital was Heshbon.

entries.section: (1) The land east of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: Moses gave this land as an inheritance to the tribe of Reuben, the tribe of Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, who wished to take their portion east of the Jordan River.
This land points to the portion of the Church of the Old Testament, which did not cross the Jordan, that is, did not receive the blessing of Baptism.

God gave His people, the tribes of Reuben and Gad and half the tribe of Manasseh, to possess the land east of the Jordan, on condition that they fight with their brothers to possess the Promised Land west of the Jordan. So if God has granted you strength and resources, help your brothers with them so that they may stand firm in the faith and triumph over Satan, and so have an inheritance in the Kingdom of Heaven.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: As for the land west of the Jordan, the Jews took it by war under the leadership of Joshua after the death of Moses and the Jews' crossing of the Jordan River. This land points to the portion of the Church of the New Testament, which enjoyed the blessing of Baptism (the crossing of the Jordan) with Joshua, who is a type of our Lord Jesus Christ. It covers the area from Baal-gad (at Caesarea Philippi) in Lebanon in the north to Mount Halak, that is, the one bare of trees, at Beersheba in the south. This land Joshua gave as a possession to the nine and a half remaining tribes of the children of Israel. It is to be noted that Joshua was humble: he did not attribute the victory to himself as the commander, but to all the people, in order to encourage everyone and make them feel God's work in them.
Take care to honor and encourage all who share with you in any work, so that they give all their effort with joy, and you protect yourself from pride and the love of praise.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: It includes the lands that were in the mountain and the valley and were inhabited by the tribes mentioned. These lands were mentioned earlier in (ch. 9, 11). Joshua was a type of Christ: just as Joshua conquered and took possession of the Promised Land, so Christ also by His death on the Cross opened for us the gates of Paradise and the Kingdom, that we may inherit with Him eternal life in the heavenly Canaan.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: Jericho: its walls fell by the power of God (ch. 6) (Map 5). Ai: before which the children of Israel were first defeated and then triumphed over it in (ch. 8). The king of Jerusalem, the king of Hebron, the king of Jarmuth, the king of Lachish, the king of Eglon: these are the five kings who went out to fight Gibeon, and Joshua defeated them and killed their kings (ch. 10), and their lands lie in the south of Palestine.
Gezer: Joshua took it after his victory over the five kings (ch. 10:33). Debir: Joshua took it after the victory over the five kings (ch. 10:38, 39). Geder: it lies in the far south of Canaan.

Hormah: it lies in the south of the land of Canaan (Num 14:45, Num 21:1-3). Arad: it lies in the south of Canaan, 17 miles from Hebron (Num 21:1). Adullam: in the south of Palestine, beside Bethlehem.
Makkedah: see (ch. 10:28). Bethel: that is, the house of God, and it lies in the south of Palestine; it is different from the Bethel mentioned in the days of the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob.
Tappuah: that is, apple, because of the abundance of apple trees in it, and it lies in the south of Palestine.
Aphek: it lies in the plain of Sharon, a fertile plain in the middle of Palestine.
Lasharon: it lies southeast of Nazareth by about five and a half miles.
Madon: it lies in the mountain in the north of Canaan, and it joined the alliance of the kings in the north to attack Joshua, but he defeated them.

Hazor: a city in the north of Canaan, whose king led the alliance against Joshua (ch. 11:1). Shimron-meron: it lies in the north of Canaan and joined the alliance, and they fought Joshua (ch. 11). Achshaph: it lies in the north of Canaan and is among the cities of the alliance (ch. 11:1). Taanach: it lies in the north of Canaan and south of the plain of Jezreel.
Megiddo: it lies in the north of Canaan and southeast of Haifa by about twenty miles. Kedesh: it lies north of Hazor in the northern part of Canaan.
Jokneam: it lies in the region of Mount Carmel in the north of Canaan.
Dor: on the Mediterranean Sea, north of Caesarea.
Goiim: it means the nations, and it lies in Gilgal beside Jericho.
Tirzah: northeast of Nabulus.
Each of these cities had a number of villages and small towns belonging to it.

The group of kings mentioned reigned over this land, and their number was thirty-one kings, each reigning over one of the cities, and Joshua defeated all of them in the wars previously recounted in the book.
The portion of the tribes east of the Jordan. From this chapter until chapter nineteen, the book makes clear the portion of each tribe from the Promised Land.

This chapter is concerned with defining, in general, the land that the Lord granted to His people west of the Jordan, and then explaining in detail the borders of each of the two and a half tribes who took their portion east of the Jordan.

(1) The remaining land west of the Jordan in general (vv. 1-7:) 1 Now Joshua was old and stricken in years; and the Lord said unto him, “Thou art old and stricken in years, and there remaineth yet very much land to be possessed. 2 This is the land that yet remaineth: all the borders of the Philistines, and all Geshuri, 3 From Sihor, which is before Egypt, even unto the borders of Ekron northward, which is counted (to the Canaanite): five lords of the Philistines; the Gazathites, and the Ashdothites, the Eshkalonites, the Gittites, and the Ekronites; also the Avites: 4 From the south, all the land of the Canaanites, and Mearah that is beside the Sidonians, unto Aphek, to the borders of the Amorites: 5 And the land of the Giblites, and all Lebanon, toward the sunrising, from Baalgad under mount Hermon unto the entering into Hamath. 6 All the inhabitants of the hill country from Lebanon unto Misrephoth-maim, and all the Sidonians, them will I drive out from before the children of Israel: only divide thou it by lot unto the Israelites for an inheritance, as I have commanded thee. 7 Now therefore divide this land for an inheritance unto the nine tribes, and the half tribe of Manasseh.”

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: Joshua had become a very old man, perhaps 107 years of age. He had spent seven years of them in his wars to possess the land of Canaan, and he had only three years of life left, for he would die at the age of 110 (ch. 24:29). So God drew his attention to the many lands in Canaan that God had given them and that they had not yet fought for and possessed, and that they must complete the possession of these lands.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: Lords: chiefs or rulers.
Before Egypt: east of Egypt and facing it.
Borders: boundaries.
Sihor: a river.
The lands that remained and that the children of Israel had not yet possessed are:

1- All the borders of the Philistines: that is, the region surrounding the southeast of the Mediterranean Sea, in which the Philistines lived, who are descended from Ham and are counted among the Canaanites.

2- The lands of the Geshurites: which lie in the south of Palestine, west of the Jordan, and are different from the land of the Geshurites that lies east of the Jordan and was possessed by the eastern half of the tribe of Manasseh in the days of Moses (ch. 12:5).
3- The great cities of Palestine, which begin from Sihor, a seasonal river lying east of Egypt and called the Wadi al-Arish, as far as the city of Ekron in the north; and they include five cities:
a- Gaza: it is the southern border of Palestine. The tribe of Judah possessed it (Judg 1:18), and the Philistines recovered it, then the Maccabees possessed it (1 Macc 13:43-48).
b- Ashdod: a fortified city, hence it was given this name, that is, strengthened and strong, and the Maccabees possessed it (1 Macc 5:68, 10:84).
c- Ashkelon: it lies 12 miles north of Gaza and is now called Asqalan.
d- Gath: a fortified city taken by David, then Rehoboam, and after him Jehoash (2 Sam 15:18, 2 Chr 11:8, 2 Kgs 13:25).

e- Ekron: it is the northern border of these cities and lies about 12 miles south of Joppa. God's people possessed it in the days of Joshua (ch. 15:45) and then in the days of Samuel (1 Sam 7:14), but afterwards the Philistines took it (Map 6).
4- The Avites: who lived near Gaza and were counted among the Philistines and then among the Canaanites. Joppa, Ashdod, Ashkelon, Gath, Palestine, Gaza. Map (6)

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: Teman: the south.

He continues the lands that the children of Israel had not possessed, saying that the land extends southward to include the homeland of all the Canaanite tribes, then northward from the cave of the Sidonians, in whose mountain there are many caves, and they reached the city of Aphek, which lies north of Sidon in Libnah. The ancient land of the Amorites was south of Jerusalem, and some of them migrated to the east of the Jordan; their kings were Sihon and Og, and the children of Israel also possessed their country that was east of the Jordan (Num 21).

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: He also adds to the lands that they had not possessed the two mountains. The land of the Giblites lies 30 kilometers north of Beirut, and it is a Phoenician land, that is, Lebanon. It is the northern border of the land that God wished to give to His people; they are not Canaanites. As for Hamath, it lies north of Damascus in Syria. And Baal-gad is Caesarea Philippi, or Baalbek in Lebanon.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: And the land of the inhabitants of the mountains, from Misrephoth beside Sidon to the border of Lebanon. The Lord promises to drive them out Himself before the Jews, to clear the land for them, on condition that Joshua divide it to them by lot, so that Joshua would not be accused of favoring any of the tribes.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: The nine tribes, in addition to the half tribe of Manasseh, take their possession in this land, because the tribes of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh had taken their possession east of the Jordan in the days of Moses (Num 32).

We must be content with what the Lord has given us of spiritual and material gifts and blessings, and not accuse circumstances or others of favoritism and of standing against us, but invest what we have received without murmuring.

(2) The portions east of the Jordan (vv. 8-14:) 8 With whom the Reubenites and the Gadites have received their inheritance, which Moses gave them, beyond Jordan eastward, even as Moses the servant of the Lord gave them; 9 From Aroer, that is upon the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain of Medeba unto Dibon; 10 And all the cities of Sihon king of the Amorites, which reigned in Heshbon, unto the border of the children of Ammon; 11 And Gilead, and the border of the Geshurites and Maachathites, and all mount Hermon, and all Bashan unto Salcah; 12 All the kingdom of Og in Bashan, which reigned in Ashtaroth and in Edrei, who remained of the remnant of the giants: for these did Moses smite, and cast them out. 13 Nevertheless the children of Israel expelled not the Geshurites, nor the Maachathites: but the Geshurites and the Maachathites dwell among the Israelites until this day. 14 Only unto the tribe of Levi he gave none inheritance; the sacrifices of the Lord God of Israel made by fire are his inheritance, as he said unto them.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: With whom: with the rest of the tribes that took possession west of the Jordan, the Reubenites and the Gadites and the half tribe of Manasseh took possession east of the Jordan.

Moses gave this land to the tribe of Reuben in the south, Gad in the middle, and the half tribe of Manasseh in the north, but they crossed over to fight with the rest of the people in the west, and they did not settle in it until the wars had ended and Joshua handed it over to them.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: Aroer: it lies on the Arnon River, on the southern border of the kingdom of Sihon.
The city that is in the midst of the valley: what is meant is Heshbon or Arnon.
The plain of Medeba: it lies 14 miles east of the Dead Sea, and around it are many lakes.
Dibon: north of the Arnon River, at a distance of 3 miles.
Heshbon: it lies between the Arnon and Jabbok rivers and was the capital of King Sihon.

He defines the land east of the Jordan with its cities, mountains and rivers, from the Dead Sea and the border of Moab in the south to the border of the Ammonites in the east, and the border of Bashan alongside the Sea of Tiberias in the north. King Og was of the descendants of a people called the Rephaim (Maps 5, 7). Ashtaroth, Jericho. Map (7)

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: But the people did not carry out the commandment of Moses to drive out the rest of the pagan peoples such as the Geshurites and the Maachathites; rather they left them among them, either out of fear of them or out of a desire that they serve them as slaves and pay them tribute.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: No land was given to the tribe of Levi; rather the rest of the tribes gave it cities for dwelling only (Num 35), as will be mentioned later, so that they would be spread out among the people to serve them spiritually, and so as not to be occupied with ownership at the expense of spiritual work. They lived from their share that they took from the sacrifices, that is, the offerings presented in the house of the Lord.

Do not be lax with evil, and do not let any image or form of it remain with you after your repentance, as the children of Israel were lax and did not drive out the pagan peoples living among them, because the devil is ready to lie in wait and be silent for a time, then return to attack you; so do not give him an opportunity.

(3) The portion of the tribe of Reuben (vv. 15-23:) 15 And Moses gave unto the tribe of the children of Reuben inheritance according to their families. 16 And their coast was from Aroer, that is on the bank of the river Arnon, and the city that is in the midst of the river, and all the plain by Medeba; 17 Heshbon, and all her cities that are in the plain; Dibon, and Bamothbaal, and Bethbaalmeon, 18 And Jahaza, and Kedemoth, and Mephaath, 19 And Kirjathaim, and Sibmah, and Zarethshahar in the mount of the valley, 20 And Bethpeor, and Ashdothpisgah, and Bethjeshimoth, 21 And all the cities of the plain, and all the kingdom of Sihon king of the Amorites, which reigned in Heshbon, whom Moses smote with the princes of Midian, Evi, and Rekem, and Zur, and Hur, and Reba, which were dukes of Sihon, dwelling in the country. 22 Balaam also the son of Beor, the soothsayer, did the children of Israel slay with the sword among them that were slain by them. 23 And the border of the children of Reuben was Jordan, and the border thereof. This was the inheritance of the children of Reuben after their families, the cities and the villages thereof.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: Families: households.
Villages thereof: the farms and villages belonging to the large city.
Bamoth-baal: a city lying north of the Arnon River and south of Mount Nebo (Num 21:19, 22:21), and the meaning of its name is the heights of Baal.
Baal: a famous pagan god.
Beth-baal-meon: it lies a few miles south of Heshbon.
Jahaza: a city lying twelve miles east of the Dead Sea. Kedemoth: it lies in the valley of the Arnon River.
Kirjathaim: about two and a half miles north of the Arnon River.
Sibmah: it lies beside Heshbon, at a distance of two miles.
Zareth-shahar: it lies east of the Dead Sea at the mouth of the Zarqa River.
Beth-peor: that is, the temple of Peor, where the house and altar of Baal-peor were, beside the top of Pisgah (Deut 4:

46.(The plains of Pisgah: one of the peaks of the mountains of Abarim, which lie northeast of the Dead Sea (Deut 34:1). Beth-jeshimoth: it lies northeast of the Dead Sea at the mouth of the Jordan River into the sea (Num 33:49). The cities of the plain: the plain lying between the Arnon and Jabbok rivers.
The princes of Sihon: the allies of King Sihon and his helpers, because the land of Midian was adjacent to King Sihon.
Jordan and the border thereof: that is, the lands lying east of the Jordan River.

The borders of the portion of the tribe of Reuben are Moab in the south, the portion of the tribe of Gad in the north, the Ammonites in the east, and the Dead Sea in the west, including the cities and villages in it (Maps 5, 7). Here is mentioned Balaam the son of Beor, whom Balak king of Moab hired to curse the Jews, but God blessed them, and the Jews killed him when they took possession of the land (Num 22-25).

Evil always returns upon the one who does it: Balaam's counsel, by which he caused the children of Israel to fall into adultery and idol worship, turned into the destruction of Balaam himself. So beware of giving bad counsel, or of having a personal aim and benefit in your guidance of others. That is, be careful to proclaim the voice of God and not your own thoughts.

(4) The portion of the tribe of Gad (vv. 24-28:) 24 And Moses gave inheritance unto the tribe of Gad, even unto the children of Gad according to their families. 25 And their coast was Jazer, and all the cities of Gilead, and half the land of the children of Ammon, unto Aroer that is before Rabbah; 26 And from Heshbon unto Ramathmizpeh, and Betonim; and from Mahanaim unto the border of Debir; 27 And in the valley, Betharam, and Bethnimrah, and Succoth, and Zaphon, the rest of the kingdom of Sihon king of Heshbon, Jordan and his border, even unto the edge of the sea of Chinnereth on the other side Jordan eastward. 28 This is the inheritance of the children of Gad after their families, the cities, and their villages.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: Jazer: a city with fertile land in Gilead (Num 21:32). Rabbah: the city of Amman, the present capital of Jordan.
Ramath-mizpeh: it is Ramoth in Gilead (Deut 4:43). Mahanaim: it lies east of the Jordan River.
Debir: it lies beside Mahanaim.
Beth-aram: it lies in the region of the plains of Moab.
Beth-nimrah: it lies east of the Jordan, opposite Jericho.
Succoth: it lies about a mile south of the Jabbok River.
Samon: it lies eight miles northeast of the mouth of the Jabbok River.

The sea of Chinnereth: it is the Lake of Gennesaret, or the Sea of Galilee, or Lake Tiberias, through which the Jordan River passes (Num 34:11). The portion of the tribe of Gad lay between the portion of the half tribe of Manasseh in the north and the portion of the tribe of Reuben in the south, and the rest of the land of the Ammonites in the east, after the sons of Gad took from the Amorites the land that the Amorites had earlier taken from the Ammonites; as for the western border of their portion, it is the Jordan River (Map 5).

God has prepared for you a portion in the Kingdom of Heaven. I wish you would take care to prepare for it so as to attain it and rejoice in it with God, and not be distracted from it by the passing concerns of the world; that is, set limits to your concerns and give sufficient time to your relationship with God.

(5) The portion of the half tribe of Manasseh (vv. 29-33:) 29 And Moses gave inheritance unto the half tribe of Manasseh: and this was the possession of the half tribe of the children of Manasseh by their families.

30 And their coast was from Mahanaim, all Bashan, all the kingdom of Og king of Bashan, and all the towns of Jair, which are in Bashan, threescore cities: 31 And half Gilead, and Ashtaroth, and Edrei, cities of the kingdom of Og in Bashan, were pertaining unto the children of Machir the son of Manasseh, even to the one half of the children of Machir by their families. 32 These are the countries which Moses did distribute for inheritance in the plains of Moab, on the other side Jordan, by Jericho, eastward. 33 But unto the tribe of Levi Moses gave not any inheritance: the Lord God of Israel was their inheritance, as he said unto them.

entries.section: (2) The land west of the Jordan River

paragraphs.text: Machir: the only son of Manasseh, and half of his descendants lived east of the Jordan and the other half west of it (Num 26:29, 1 Chr 7:14). The land of Bashan: it is the one ruled by Og (Num 21:31-35). Towns: farms, and what is meant is the agricultural cities and villages that Jair the son of Manasseh conquered.
Jair: he was of the tribe of Judah but was ascribed to the tribe of Manasseh because he married a woman of the descendants of Machir.
Half Gilead: the tribe of Manasseh took possession of it, and the other half was taken by the Reubenites and the Gadites.

Ashtaroth: a capital of the kingdom of Og, lying east of the Sea of Galilee at a distance of 21 miles (Num 21:33). Edrei: another capital of King Og, lying southeast of the Sea of Galilee at a distance of 29 miles (Num 21:33). To the one half of the children of Machir: because the other half took its portion near the Jordan.

The portion of the half tribe of Manasseh, who are of the descendants of Machir, was from the land of Bashan, good for pasture, in the north to the portion of the tribe of Gad in the south, and from the north of the land of Ammon in the east to the Jordan River and the Lake of Tiberias in the west (Map 7). The cities of the sons of Levi were distributed throughout the whole land, as mentioned before, and they took them only to dwell in, but they did not possess a portion of the lands like the rest of the tribes, because they were consecrated to the service of God, so their portion was the Lord, and this is the greatest thing.

God cares for those consecrated to His service and provides for them. And if you offer service to God, be confident that He blesses you spiritually and materially and cares for your needs, because you have become one of His servants and His special followers.
The portion of Caleb

entries.section: (1) The general division of the land

paragraphs.text: These: it refers to the lands that the children of Israel possessed west of the Jordan.

The distribution of the land took place in the presence of Eleazar the priest, the third son of Aaron, and Joshua, whom Moses had appointed ruler over the people, and likewise the heads of the tribes, one from each tribe. The name of Eleazar is put before Joshua here because Moses had ordained him ruler over the people in the presence of Eleazar the priest.

entries.section: (1) The general division of the land

paragraphs.text: The distribution of the portions was by lot: the names of the tribes were written down and the portions were written down, and one was drawn from each, so that the portion was determined (Num 26:53, 33:54, 55). As for the Levites, they did not take a portion of the land; rather the Lord would give them cities to dwell in among the rest of the tribes (ch. 13:14, 33).

entries.section: (1) The general division of the land

paragraphs.text: Suburbs: pastures.
Their substance: their servants and their sheep.

Joseph became two tribes, and so the tribe of Levi had no portion. In this way Joseph enjoyed a double portion, which is the portion of the firstborn with regard to his father Jacob, and so the words of Moses were carried out in dividing the lands among the tribes.

Joseph's receiving two tribes and his being counted the firstborn of Jacob instead of Reuben was because Joseph was righteous, whereas Reuben sinned with his father's concubine and lost the blessing (Gen 35:21). So the tribes numbered twelve, because the Levites did not take a portion, and Joseph took their place by receiving two tribes, and the Levites took from each tribe cities to dwell in, with fields and pastures around them for their flocks, as mentioned in (Num 35).

The blessing of the Lord is great for the one who fears Him, like Joseph. So enjoy your relationship with God; then He provides all your needs, and even blesses you more than you imagine, and you rejoice in His fellowship.
The Kenezite: the Kenezites are a Canaanite tribe, from which Caleb may have come and become a Jew, or one of his ancestors was called Kenaz and was of Jewish origin.

Gilgal: a region south of Jericho lying on the Dead Sea, which was Joshua's headquarters (Map 1). Caleb came forward with a group from the tribe of Judah to Joshua; Caleb was the head of the tribe of Judah (Num 34:19), and a group of them came with him to support him in his request. Caleb reminded Joshua of Moses' praise of them both when they returned from spying out the land, and their encouraging the people to enter it, and of his promise to them of a portion in the land. It is understood from this that they had a distinction in the possession of the land because of their obedience to God and their encouraging the people (Num 13, 14).

Caleb was 40 years old when he went with Joshua from Kadesh to spy out the land, and he returned and testified truthfully to the greatness of God's promise to His people of this splendid land, for it is a land full of good things and God is able to lead His people and give them possession of this land.
Made melt: disturbed and terrified the children of Israel.

As for the rest of the spies, besides Caleb and Joshua, they turned aside from the way of God and frightened the people from entering the land of Canaan because of the strength of those who lived in it.
When Caleb spied out the land of Canaan, he entered the region of Hebron, that is, his feet trod upon it, and Moses promised him on his return from spying that he would take this land.
Thirty-eight years passed in the journey in the wilderness and seven years in the wars of Canaan with Joshua, and Caleb reached the age of 85.

Caleb had reached the age of 85, which is an advanced age, but his piety and love of God gave him a spiritual zeal that strengthened his body, so that he was ready for war and for possessing the land like any young man, that is, as he was in his strength at the age of 40 when he spied out the land.
The mountain: what is meant is the city of Hebron and the mountainous region surrounding it.
The Anakim: one of the tribes of Canaan, distinguished by tall stature and strength.
Thou heardest: the spies' frightening of the people so that the people would not enter it, because of the strength of its inhabitants, the Anakim and other tribes of Canaan.
Therefore he asks for his portion in the high mountain that the Anakim inhabited, so that he may drive them out and dwell in their place according to God's promise to him.

Hebron is the city of Al-Khalil, in which the fathers Abraham, Isaac and Jacob and their wives are buried. It became Caleb's possession, but he afterwards gave it up, and it became one of the cities of the Levites (Josh 21:13).
Hebron was first called Kirjath-arba, and Arba was the father of Anak, to whom the Anakim are ascribed; then Caleb changed its name to Hebron, after one of his descendants.
As a result of the peoples' fear of the Jews, they ceased to stir up war with them, and the land had rest.

Take courage in your spiritual striving, for you have a great portion of blessing with Christ. Fight by the grace of God and you will triumph and rejoice. Leave your sins and persevere in your striving to acquire virtue, knowing that you will triumph by the power of Christ.

The portion of the tribe of Judah. From here begins the distribution of the portions of three diligent tribes, namely the tribe of Judah (ch. 15), the tribe of Ephraim (ch. 16) and the half tribe of Manasseh (ch. 17). This distribution took place at Gilgal, and we begin with the portion of the tribe of Judah.

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Judah

paragraphs.text: According to their families: it includes all the families of the tribe.
Teman: the south.
Tongue: the bay.
The Salt Sea: the Dead Sea.

Joshua began the distribution of the land from the south to the north, and it was done by lot. God chose the tribe of Judah as the first of the tribes in the lot because it was the most pious of the tribes, and from it Christ came forth; the Temple was in its land, and its kingship lasted longer than that of the other tribes, so it went into captivity as the last of the tribes.

The borders of Judah were very wide, and these verses include the southern borders of the tribe of Judah, which is the country of Edom, the descendants of Esau, who lived in the mountains of Seir, and “the wilderness of Zin,” which adjoins the mountains of Seir and lies on the southern border of the land of Judah. The border of Judah extends to the farthest, that is, the last part of the Dead Sea in the south, which is a bay (Map 8). The border extended southward to “the ascent of Akrabbim”; ascent means a rough road on the mountain, and Akrabbim means scorpions, and it was called so because of the many scorpions in it. Beyond it to the west is the wilderness of Zin, which is part of the wilderness of Paran extending north of the wilderness of Sinai.

It passes south of Kadesh-barnea, then reaches a village called Hezron beside Kadesh-barnea, and goes up to a neighboring village higher than it called Addar, then turns to a low part in the wilderness of Zin called Karkaa, then reaches Azmon, which is northwest of the wilderness of Sinai, then passes beside the river of Egypt, meaning the Wadi al-Arish, which is the valley of a seasonal river that fills with rain in the rainy season and flows into the Mediterranean Sea. What is meant by the goings out of the border is the end of the southern border of the tribe of Judah, which is the sea, that is, the Mediterranean Sea. So the southern border extends east from the south of the Dead Sea and extends west to the Mediterranean Sea.
Map (8)

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Judah

paragraphs.text: This verse tells us of the eastern border of the tribe of Judah, which is the Dead Sea, that is, “the Salt Sea,” to its end in the north, that is, at the mouth of the Jordan River into it.

In this verse he also begins to make clear the northern border of the tribe of Judah, which begins from the tongue, that is, the bay that lies north of the Dead Sea and into which the Jordan River flows, that is, the uttermost part of the Jordan.

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Judah

paragraphs.text: He continues the northern border of the tribe of Judah. The border passes by Beth-hogla, which lies east of Jericho, then passes through a plain called Beth-arabah, then the stone of Bohan, then passes the valley of Achor, which lies south of Jericho and was so named because of the sin of Achan the son of Carmi, and after that reaches the village of Debir, which is Kirjath-sepher (v. 15). After that the border turns north to reach “Gilgal,” where the tabernacle of meeting was set up and which was the headquarters of Joshua the son of Nun. Gilgal is opposite a region called “the going up to Adummim,” which separates the borders of Judah and Benjamin, and it passes south of a valley that separates Judah and Benjamin. Then it passes the waters of En-shemesh, a spring of water lying three miles east of Jerusalem and separating the borders of Judah and Benjamin. Then the border reaches its farthest point at En-rogel, which lies near Jerusalem and also separates the land of Judah and Benjamin. Then it turns to the valley of the son of Hinnom, which lies southwest of Jerusalem. The Jebusite means the Jebusites, the original inhabitants of Jerusalem. Then the border goes up on the mountain that lies opposite the region in which the Rephaim live, a people of giants among the original inhabitants of the land, and perhaps this mountain is Mount Zion, which lies beside Jerusalem.

Then the border extends to the well of Nephtoah, which is on the border of Judah and Benjamin, then to Mount Ephron, which is also on the border of Judah and Benjamin. After that it extends to the village of Baalah, which is Kirjath-jearim, and the Gibeonites lived in it (ch. 9:17). Then it extends to Mount Seir, then to Mount Jearim, then to Beth-shemesh and Timnah, all on the northern border of Judah.

Then it extends to Mount Ekron and from it to Shicron, then across Mount Baalah, and from it to the city of Jabneel, which lies 6 km east of the Mediterranean Sea and was a center of learning, where the highest assembly of the Jews, that is, the Sanhedrin, met. Then the border extends to reach the Mediterranean Sea.

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Judah

paragraphs.text: The western border of Judah is the Mediterranean Sea.

Keep borders for your life that you do not overstep to take the rights of others, so that you respect their right not only in material things but also in speech and conduct. In this way you live in peace with others and hurt no one's feelings.

entries.section: (2) Caleb's portion in the midst of Judah

paragraphs.text: Caleb took his portion directly, before and outside the lot, according to the commandment of Moses the prophet. As explained earlier, he took Kirjath-arba the father of Anak, which is Hebron, and the mountain with its caves (ch. 14:12).

entries.section: (2) Caleb's portion in the midst of Judah

paragraphs.text: With strong faith Caleb drove out the Anakim with their three families.

entries.section: (2) Caleb's portion in the midst of Judah

paragraphs.text: Caleb came to the village of Kirjath-sepher, and promised that whoever drove its inhabitants out of it, he would give him his daughter Achsah as a wife. It is understood from this that many young men wished to be joined to his daughter, and he wanted to marry her to the one among them most courageous, most able to bear responsibility, and most loving of God.

entries.section: (2) Caleb's portion in the midst of Judah

paragraphs.text: Othniel took the city of Debir, so Caleb gave him his daughter Achsah as a wife. Othniel was probably Caleb's brother or his brother's son, and Othniel became one of the judges of the children of Israel and delivered his people from the Aramaeans (Judg 3:8-11).

entries.section: (2) Caleb's portion in the midst of Judah

paragraphs.text: As she came to him: when she was being brought in procession to her bridegroom on her way to her new home.
She moved him: she encouraged him and urged him on.
The upper springs and the nether springs: springs that flow from high lands and from low lands.

During the wedding procession of Achsah the daughter of Caleb, before she reached her home, she encouraged her husband to ask a blessing from her father, and it seems that he was shy, so she came forward to ask this blessing from her father herself, which was the request for a field. Although she did not ask for a new piece of land, she asked for springs to water the lands that she and her husband had possessed, which are worthless if there are no sources of water to irrigate them; with this water she would have acquired a field. Note her respect for her father: she got down from the donkey she was riding on her way to her home and asked her father for this blessing, and he gave it to her (Judg 1:8-15).

Everyone who asks finds, and to him who knocks it is opened. Ask God to change your weaknesses into strength, and He will give and will not reproach. Just as Achsah asked from her father, ask from your heavenly Father, and trust in His fatherhood and love that He will give you all your needs.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: We shall mention here the cities whose location is now certain; as for the rest of the cities, there are differing opinions about their location.
The uttermost ... southward: those on the southern border of the portion of the tribe of Judah, which were beside the border of the country of Edom.
Villages: hamlets.
Adar: it is now Adar, which lies south of Gaza at a distance of 7.5 km.
Hazor (v. 23:) There are many places by the name of Hazor or Hezron, which means an enclosure, since enclosures for cattle were set up there.
Shema: it lies in the Negev and is now called Tell Sufa.

Beersheba: it lies about 45 km south of Galilee, and it is where Abraham made a covenant with Abimelech and sacrificed seven ewe lambs as proof of his ownership of the neighboring well (Gen 21:31). Kadesh: it is either Kadesh-barnea, from which Moses sent the spies to spy out the Promised Land (Num 13:26), or another Kadesh, since there are many cities by this name. The meaning of Kadesh is holy, since in the cities called Kadesh places for the worship of idols were set up.
Kerioth: it is the hometown of Judas Iscariot, that is, he was of the same tribe as Christ (the tribe of Judah), but he sold his Master.

Here are mentioned 38 cities lying in the south of the portion of the tribe of Judah, beside the Edomites and the Arab tribes, but the tribe of Simeon took nine cities from Judah because its own portion was too small for it (ch. 19:1-9), so the tribe of Judah was left with only 29 cities in the south.

(b) The plain region in the portion of Judah (vv. 33-47:) 33 And in the valley, Eshtaol, and Zoreah, and Ashnah, 34 And Zanoah, and Engannim, Tappuah, and Enam, 35 Jarmuth, and Adullam, Socoh, and Azekah, 36 And Sharaim, and Adithaim, and Gederah, and Gederothaim; fourteen cities with their villages: 37 Zenan, and Hadashah, and Migdalgad, 38 And Dilean, and Mizpeh, and Joktheel, 39 Lachish, and Bozkath, and Eglon, 40 And Cabbon, and Lahmam, and Kithlish, 41 And Gederoth, Bethdagon, and Naamah, and Makkedah; sixteen cities with their villages: 42 Libnah, and Ether, and Ashan, 43 And Jiphtah, and Ashnah, and Nezib, 44 And Keilah, and Achzib, and Mareshah; nine cities with their villages: 45 Ekron, with her towns and her villages: 46 From Ekron westward, all that lay near Ashdod, with their villages:
47 Ashdod with her towns and her villages, Gaza with her towns and her villages, unto the river of Egypt, and the great sea, and the border thereof.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: Eshtaol: it lies about 12 km west of Jerusalem.
Zoreah: it still has its name to this day and lies about 22.5 km west of Jerusalem.
Ashnah: it lies about 25 km northwest of Jerusalem.
Adullam: it lies beside Bethlehem.
The valley (v. 33): it is the low land lying in the middle of the land of Canaan.
Here are mentioned 14 cities with their villages, that is, the villages surrounding them, and they lie in the plain in the midst of the portion of Judah.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: He continues the cities lying in the plain in the midst of the portion of the tribe of Judah, and mentions 16 cities with their suburbs.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: Here he mentions nine cities with their villages, also lying in the middle plain in the portion of the tribe of Judah.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: Ekron: one of the great Philistine cities and the seat of the god Baal-zebub; it lies about 19 km south of Joppa.
Ashdod: one of the great Philistine cities, and the seat of the god Dagon; the meaning of its name is strength or power, and it lies 18 miles northeast of Gaza.
Gaza: one of the great Philistine cities, lying near the Mediterranean Sea (ch. 13:
3.(The river of Egypt: the valley of the seasonal river Al-Arish, which is not the valley of the Nile.
The great sea: the Mediterranean Sea.
Here are mentioned three large cities in the portion of the tribe of Judah, lying in the west of its portion toward the Mediterranean Sea.
Thus the total of the cities lying in the plain is 42 cities.

(c) The hill country in the portion of Judah (vv. 48-59:) 48 And in the mountains, Shamir, and Jattir, and Socoh, 49 And Dannah, and Kirjathsannah (which is Debir), 50 And Anab, and Eshtemoh, and Anim, 51 And Goshen, and Holon, and Giloh; eleven cities with their villages: 52 Arab, and Dumah, and Eshean, 53 And Janum, and Bethtappuah, and Aphekah, 54 And Humtah, and Kirjatharba (which is Hebron), and Zior; nine cities with their villages: 55 Maon, Carmel, and Ziph, and Juttah, 56 And Jezreel, and Jokdeam, and Zanoah, 57 Cain, Gibeah, and Timnah; ten cities with their villages: 58 Halhul, Bethzur, and Gedor, 59 And Maarath, and Bethanoth, and Eltekon; six cities with their villages.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: The mountain: the high lands far from the seacoast and overlooking the valley of the Jordan River from its western bank.
Shamir: it lies 17 km west of Al-Khalil (Hebron).
Kirjath-sannah: it is Debir or Kirjath-sepher, which Othniel the son of Kenaz took (vv. 7, 15). Anab: it lies southwest of the city of Al-Khalil at a distance of 26 km.
Eshtemoh: it lies south of Al-Khalil at a distance of 15 km.
Anim: it lies south of Al-Khalil at a distance of 19 km.
The first group of the cities lying in the hill country in the lands of Judah numbers 11 cities with their villages.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: Arab: it is the village of Al-Rabiya, which lies south of the city of Al-Khalil.
Dumah: it still has its name to this day and lies southwest of the city of Al-Khalil at a distance of 19 km. Eshean: beside the city of Al-Khalil.
Janum: beside Hebron, which is Al-Khalil.
Beth-tappuah: it is now called Al-Tuffah and lies eight km west of Al-Khalil.
Humtah: a village beside the city of Al-Khalil.
Kirjath-arba: it is Hebron, now called the city of Al-Khalil (ch. 10:3). Zior: it is now called the small village (Saghir) and lies eight km northeast of Al-Khalil.
The second group of the cities lying in the hill country in the lands of Judah numbers nine cities with their villages.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: Maon: it lies on a hill south of the city of Al-Khalil at a distance of 13 km.
Ziph: it lies beside the wilderness of Ziph, 7 km southeast of Al-Khalil, and is different from the one mentioned in (v. 24). Juttah: it is the village of Yatta and lies about 9 km west of Al-Khalil.
Jokdeam: south of Al-Khalil, near Juttah.
Cain: beside Hebron.
Gibeah: it lies north of Al-Khalil at a distance of 16 km.
Timnah: it lies south of Al-Khalil.
The third group of the cities lying in the hill lands of Judah numbers ten cities with their villages.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: Halhul: it lies about 6 km north of Al-Khalil.
Beth-zur: it lies about 7 km north of Al-Khalil and still has its name to this day.
Gedor: it lies between Hebron and Bethlehem.
Maarath: it lies about 12 km north of Al-Khalil and is different from the one mentioned in (ch. 13:4). Beth-anoth: it lies about 5 km northeast of Al-Khalil.
Eltekon: it lies about 7 km west of Bethlehem.
The fourth group of the cities lying in the hill lands of Judah numbers six cities with their villages.

(d) The wilderness region in the portion of Judah (vv. 60-63:) 60 Kirjathbaal (which is Kirjathjearim), and Rabbah; two cities with their villages. 61 In the wilderness, Betharabah, Middin, and Secacah, 62 And Nibshan, and the city of Salt, and Engedi; six cities with their villages. 63 As for the Jebusites the inhabitants of Jerusalem, the children of Judah could not drive them out: but the Jebusites dwell with the children of Judah at Jerusalem unto this day.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah
