paragraphs.text: Kirjath-baal or Jearim: it was called by this name after Baal, the most famous of the gods of the Canaanites, and it lies about 15 km west of Jerusalem.
The fifth group of the cities lying in the hill lands of Judah numbers two cities with their villages.
Thus the total of the cities lying in the hill lands of Judah is 38 cities.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: The wilderness: the wilderness (v. 61) is the wilderness of Judah west of the Dead Sea and southwest of Jerusalem, in which John the Baptist grew up (Lk 3:3), and it is called the wilderness of Judea (Mt 3:1). Nibshan: it lies southeast of Jericho.

The city of Salt: it lies close to the Dead Sea, about 13 km southwest of Jericho. Engedi: it lies a mile west of the Dead Sea, and beside it is a spring of water of the same name. The wilderness of Judea includes six cities with their villages.
From this we know that the portion of Judah includes 115 cities with their villages and fields.

entries.section: (3) The cities in the portion of Judah

paragraphs.text: The Jebusites: they are the descendants of Canaan the son of Ham, that is, one of the Canaanite tribes, and they are the original inhabitants of Jerusalem. Although Joshua had overcome them, being among the five kings (ch. 11:1-12), they came back and took possession of part of Jerusalem.

The tribe of Judah was lax in driving them out, either out of fear of them, or out of laziness on the part of the tribe of Judah, or in an attempt to use them as slaves, and the rest of the tribes fell into this negligence, which led these inhabitants to rise against the Jews and humiliate them, as appears in the Book of Judges. David overcame the Jebusites and took Jerusalem and the mountain (2 Sam 5).

Continue your striving to be rid of every source of sin, and do not be lax with the smallest thing, lest it become an opening for the devil, and trust in the power of God that supports you, so that you purify yourself from every evil inclination. The portion of the tribe of Ephraim

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh in general

paragraphs.text: The Jordan by Jericho: the part of the Jordan River adjoining Jericho.

The water of Jericho: the spring adjoining Jericho whose waters the prophet Elisha healed (2 Kgs 2:19-25). Toward the sunrising: that is, the eastern border of the land of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh, which lies in the east of the land of Canaan. The wilderness: the desert adjoining Jericho.

He mentions the borders of the lands of the two sons of Joseph, that is, the tribes of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasseh who lived west of the Jordan, because the first half of the tribe of Manasseh lived east of the Jordan (Num 32). For Joseph took two portions, that is, double that of his brothers, as Jacob had promised him because of his piety and righteousness (Gen 48:5, 6). The border begins from the Jordan River adjoining Jericho and extends to the spring of Jericho, then to the desert adjoining it, which lies in the east of the land of Canaan (Map 8).

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh in general

paragraphs.text: Ataroth: a town lying south of Bethel and about 11 km north of Jerusalem, on the border between Ephraim and Benjamin.

The border extended from Bethel, which was built beside Luz and where God appeared to Jacob in the ladder, and the border extended to the city of Ataroth, in which the Archites lived, from whom came Hushai the Archite, the counselor and friend of David the prophet, who defeated the counsel of Ahithophel (2 Sam 15:32).

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh in general

paragraphs.text: The border extended westward to the Japhletites, who are among the Canaanite tribes, that is, the original inhabitants of the land. Then it extended to the city of Beth-horon, which lies on low ground, because there is a city of the same name lying on high ground, which lies 19 km north of Jerusalem. Then the border extended to Gezer beside Horon, lying about 29 km northwest of Jerusalem.
So we find that the goings out of the border of the tribe of Ephraim, that is, its beginning, are at the Dead Sea, and then it extends northward beside the Jordan River.

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribes of Ephraim and Manasseh in general

paragraphs.text: This is the portion of the tribe of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasseh, and it lies north of the portion of the tribe of Judah, and their lands were fertile.

God's blessings are many for His pious children. Just as He gave a double portion to His son Joseph, He still singles out His pious ones with spiritual and material blessings. Fear God and trust that you will enjoy greater care from Him, and He will provide all your needs.

entries.section: (2) The portion of the tribe of Ephraim

paragraphs.text: After mentioning the portion of the tribes of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasseh in general, he mentions here the borders of the portion of the tribe of Ephraim, which extended east from the city of Ataroth-addar, mentioned in (v. 2), to the upper Beth-horon, that is, the one lying on high ground (v. 3) (Map 8).

entries.section: (2) The portion of the tribe of Ephraim

paragraphs.text: The border extended westward toward the Mediterranean Sea to the town of Michmethah, then turned back and went east to Taanath-shiloh, that is, the entrance of Shiloh. Shiloh became the seat of the tabernacle of meeting until the days of Samuel the prophet, then afterwards it was moved to Nob, then Gibeon, and finally David moved it to Jerusalem. Then the border extended to the east of a town called Janohah.

entries.section: (2) The portion of the tribe of Ephraim

paragraphs.text: Then the border went down from Janohah to Ataroth. This Ataroth lies close to the Jordan River and is different from the one mentioned in (vv. 2, 5). Then it went to Naarath, which is close to Jericho in the valley of the Jordan. Then it reached the city of Jericho, lying five miles west of the Jordan, then extended to the Jordan River.

entries.section: (2) The portion of the tribe of Ephraim

paragraphs.text: The border extended to the city of Tappuah, which lies at a distance of 13 km from Nabulus, then turned west to the valley of Kanah, and the valley of Kanah is known today by the same name; the border of this valley of Kanah reaches the Mediterranean Sea at the city of Joppa. As for the border of the portion of Ephraim, it reached only the valley of Kanah and did not extend with it to the sea.

entries.section: (2) The portion of the tribe of Ephraim

paragraphs.text: The portion of the half tribe of Manasseh living west of the Jordan was large, so some of its cities were given to Ephraim his brother by Joshua's appointment and allotment, as is made clear in (ch. 17). It is to be noted that Joshua was of the tribe of Ephraim, so he took his portion in the midst of this tribe, but he did not take it until after the distribution of the portions of all the tribes, as is made clear in (ch. 19:49, 50). This shows the servant's putting his brothers before himself.

entries.section: (2) The portion of the tribe of Ephraim

paragraphs.text: The tribe of Ephraim was lax in driving the Canaanites out of its lands, and they remained living in Gezer, and the tribe used them as slaves. The rest of the tribes fell into this same error, and these pagans became a snare to the children of Israel, for they mixed with them and intermarried with them and worshiped their idols, so God abandoned them, as will appear in the Book of Judges.
I wish you would put others before yourself, whether in material distribution or in honor and praise, so that you win everyone and acquire humility and receive many blessings from God.
The portion of the western half tribe of Manasseh

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Manasseh east and west of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: Here he speaks in general terms about the portion of the tribe of Manasseh, who was the firstborn of Joseph and took a portion like the rest of Joseph's brothers, although the tribe of Ephraim his younger brother took a larger portion according to the prophecy of Jacob his grandfather (Gen 48:19). Manasseh had one son, Machir, who was distinguished as a brave man of war (Num 32:33-42), so half the tribe of Manasseh, that is, half the sons of Machir, possessed a portion east of the Jordan in the days of Moses, in the land of Gilead and Bashan. The land of Gilead is so called either after a person named Gilead who lived there anciently before the sons of Jacob, or after Gilead the son of Machir who lived in these lands east of the Jordan (Map 7).

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Manasseh east and west of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: Here he mentions the son of Machir, who is Gilead, and his six male sons.

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Manasseh east and west of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: Here he makes clear that the sixth son of Gilead is Hepher, and this Hepher begot Zelophehad and no other. And Zelophehad begot five daughters, that is, he had no male descendants.

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Manasseh east and west of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: The five daughters, who were of the descendants of Zelophehad, came forward and asked Joshua and Eleazar the priest to fulfill the promise of Moses to them to give them a portion in the land of Canaan like the rest of their cousins (Num 27, 36:10-12).

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Manasseh east and west of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: In this way the tribe of Manasseh received ten portions that it possessed west of the Jordan, five of them for his five sons and the other five for the daughters of Zelophehad, so the total portion of Manasseh west of the Jordan is ten portions, that is, shares.

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Manasseh east and west of the Jordan

paragraphs.text: In this way the daughters of Zelophehad possessed lands within the tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan, on condition that they marry their cousins so that their portion would not pass out of the tribe of Manasseh. This is in addition to the portion of Manasseh east of the Jordan.
Demand your right and God will help you, especially when you demand your spiritual rights, to receive a portion and membership in the Church, so that you enjoy God's care and peace.

entries.section: (2) The land of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan and its cities

paragraphs.text: Asher: a city about 25 km east of Shechem (Nabulus).
Michmethah: a city lying beside Shechem to the east.

This land corresponds to the part lying east of the Jordan, and it is bounded on the north by the portion of the tribes of Issachar and Asher, on the south by the portion of Ephraim, and on the west by the Mediterranean Sea. Shechem, which is present-day Nabulus, is counted among the most important cities; in it are the bones of Joseph, and in it were the tents of Abraham and Jacob, and in it Joshua read the Law to the people. Shechem became the capital of Israel (the northern kingdom) in the days of Jeroboam the son of Nebat, and it was defiled by him and by his idols, whose worship he introduced into Israel.
The border extends from the east to a town called Asher, then Michmethah, and after that to Shechem, then turns to the right, that is, to the south, to reach the town of Tappuah (ch. 16:8).

entries.section: (2) The land of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan and its cities

paragraphs.text: The tribe of Manasseh possessed the lands surrounding the city of Tappuah. As for the city of Tappuah itself, it belonged to the tribe of Ephraim.

entries.section: (2) The land of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan and its cities

paragraphs.text: The border extended southward, heading to the south of the valley of Kanah, and this valley of Kanah is a vast plain extending to the Mediterranean Sea. There was a watercourse passing between the cities of Manasseh. It is to be noted that in this region the cities of Manasseh are mixed with the cities of Ephraim (Map 8).

entries.section: (2) The land of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan and its cities

paragraphs.text: Here he confirms the position of the portion of Manasseh among the tribes: the portion of Ephraim was south of the valley of Kanah, while the portion of the tribe of Manasseh was north of this valley, that is, the portion of Ephraim lies south of the portion of Manasseh, and in the west of the portion of Manasseh lies the Mediterranean Sea, while on its north was the tribe of Asher on the western side and the tribe of Issachar in the northeast.

entries.section: (2) The land of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan and its cities

paragraphs.text: The tribe of Manasseh was numerous, so Joshua gave it some cities lying on the border between it and the tribes of Issachar and Asher lying to its north. These cities are:
Beth-shean: it is now Beisan, which is 6 km from the Jordan River, together with its villages and fields. Ibleam: beside the city of Jenin.

Dor: a city lying on the Mediterranean Sea (ch. 11:2, 12:23). Endor: it lies 9 km southeast of Nazareth. In it was the witch to whom Saul went, and there the prophet Samuel appeared to him (1 Sam 28:7). Taanach: it lay within the borders of Issachar.
Megiddo: it was a great city with an ancient civilization.
The three heights: what is meant is the last three cities, which were built on high ground, and in them the worship of the pagan gods was offered on the high places.

entries.section: (2) The land of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan and its cities

paragraphs.text: The tribe of Manasseh was lax and afraid, so it did not drive out the Canaanite inhabitants from these lands, but lived with them.

entries.section: (2) The land of the half tribe of Manasseh west of the Jordan and its cities

paragraphs.text: After the tribe of Manasseh grew strong, it was content to take tribute from the pagan inhabitants of the land, and this is a great error, as we mentioned, into which the children of Israel fell. So they mixed and intermarried with them and worshiped their idols, and God was angry with them and humbled them and strengthened the original inhabitants of the land against them, as appears from the Book of Judges.

If God gives you strength and zeal for life with Him, do not be lax and lose this opportunity, but rise and drive out from yourself your old evil thoughts and bad habits, for God supports you and awaits your love and your rejection of evil for His sake.

entries.section: (3) The demand for a larger portion

paragraphs.text: One lot: although Joshua had given them two portions, that is, a portion for Manasseh and a portion for Ephraim, yet joined together they express the smallness of this portion by saying one lot and one portion, that is, it is small, as if it were one portion.

The sons of Joseph joined together, the number of the sons of Manasseh being 52,700 persons and of the sons of Ephraim 34,500 according to the census of the Book of Numbers (ch. 26), and they came forward complaining to Joshua, asking for additional space in the land because of their large number.

entries.section: (3) The demand for a larger portion

paragraphs.text: Mount Ephraim: a mountainous region with fruit-bearing trees lying in the midst of the portion of the tribe of Ephraim. The mountain was so called because it lies in the portion of Ephraim and because it has fruit trees on it, since the word Ephraim means fruitful.

Joshua asked them to go to the forests in the high mountains of Ephraim and cut down the trees that bear no fruit in the land of the Perizzites and the Rephaim, and destroy its original inhabitants living in the midst of the forests, who are the Perizzites and the Rephaim, so that it would become land fit for dwelling and they could dwell in it.

entries.section: (3) The demand for a larger portion

paragraphs.text: They objected that the Canaanites were strong, armed with chariots of iron, so they could not drive them out and possess their lands, nor could they live with them, for the mountain would not hold them both. This shows Ephraim's weak faith in the power of God, who is able to support them in driving out the enemies.

entries.section: (3) The demand for a larger portion

paragraphs.text: Joshua said that these two great tribes really needed additional land, which they would obtain by their own effort from the lands of the mountain, and he made clear to them that the mountain and its outgoings, that is, what lies beyond it, were theirs, and that the iron chariots cannot travel on the mountain and in the forests on it, but travel only in the level valley, so there is nothing to fear from them there.
By this Joshua stirs them up to rely on God and go forward, because they are a great people, and to drive out the Canaanite tribes living there.
We often make excuses of weakness, as Satan deceives us about the danger of striving. But we can do all things in Christ who strengthens us.
The portion of the tribe of Benjamin

The congregation of the children of Israel assembled, that is, the Jews belonging to the seven tribes that had not yet possessed land, and their assembly was in a city called Shiloh, which is a city in the middle of the Promised Land, and they set up the tabernacle of meeting there so that it would be easy for all the tribes to reach it. The tabernacle of meeting had previously been at Gilgal for about six years, which is beside Jericho and the Jordan River, and the tabernacle of meeting remained about 300 years at Shiloh until the Philistines seized the ark of the covenant in the days of Eli the priest and Samuel the prophet (1 Sam 4); then David brought the ark of the covenant back to Jerusalem and set up the tabernacle there (2 Sam 6). The assembly of the children of Israel before the tabernacle of meeting was so that the division would take place in the presence of the Lord. The Canaanite tribes had submitted to the children of Israel and surrendered, and some fled, but some regions were still possessed by these tribes. So the submission was partial and not complete, and the land would be divided on condition that each tribe complete the driving out of the remaining Canaanites.

The seven remaining tribes are: Benjamin, Simeon, Zebulun, Issachar, Asher, Naphtali and Dan, and they will take their portion as mentioned in (ch. 18, 19), because the other five tribes took their portion east and west of the Jordan as mentioned in the preceding chapters.

Joshua rebuked the rest of the tribes for their laziness in possessing their portion in the land of Canaan and in clearing the remaining parts of the Canaanite inhabitants, because God's promise is true: He had given it to them, that is, He is ready to help them in possessing the land and driving the wicked out of it.
Joshua's rebuke is a type of the rebuke of Christ Jesus to those invited who excused themselves from attending the wedding (Mt 22:3).
I wish you would begin every work with prayer so that God may intervene, and know that prayer does not make unnecessary the work that follows it, but blesses it.

entries.section: (2) The choosing of delegates for the division

paragraphs.text: Describe it according to their inheritances: divide the land into seven parts so that each part may take a portion of it by lot.

Joshua asked the heads of the seven tribes to choose three men distinguished by diligence and precision, so that a group of 21 men would be formed to survey the remaining land of Canaan and divide it into seven parts to be distributed by lot to the seven remaining tribes.

entries.section: (2) The choosing of delegates for the division

paragraphs.text: After the remaining land is divided into seven parts to be distributed among the tribes, the tribe of Judah would be in the south of the land of Canaan, and north of it would lie the house of Joseph, that is, the tribes of Ephraim and the half tribe of Manasseh that possessed land west of the Jordan, because the other half tribe of Manasseh possessed land east of the Jordan.

entries.section: (2) The choosing of delegates for the division

paragraphs.text: The method of division was carried out by surveying the land in all its regions and writing a description of its contents of cities, rivers, farms, pastures and valleys, then casting the lot so that God would determine for each tribe a region of the land.

entries.section: (2) The choosing of delegates for the division

paragraphs.text: As for the Levites, they have no portion in the land, but are given cities with their pastures to live among the tribes in the land of Canaan, as will come in (ch. 21). And we do not forget that two and a half tribes had received their portion east of the Jordan from the hand of Moses.

entries.section: (2) The choosing of delegates for the division

paragraphs.text: Book: a writing.

The delegates did that as Joshua said. It is clear that they had learned the principles of surveying and measurement from the Egyptians during their sojourn in Egypt, and they brought what they had written to Joshua so that he might cast the lot before the Lord and determine the place of each tribe.
God's grace and protection of this group appear, for the owners of the pagan land did not molest them.
In the division, not only the area was taken into account, but also the extent of the good things of the land, in water and crops, that is, in all respects.
And after the division by lot, Joshua took into account the number of each tribe, so he gave the large tribe in number a larger area, taking it from the tribes smaller in number.

Know that God chooses for you your position in life, so do not murmur or worry, for you are the right person in the right place according to God's plan for your salvation and the salvation of the world.

entries.section: (3) The portion of the tribe of Benjamin

paragraphs.text: Beth-aven: it lies about 9.5 km east of Bethel (ch. 7:2). Luz: Bethel, lying midway between Jerusalem and Nabulus.

Ataroth-adar: it lies about 11 km north of Jerusalem (ch. 16:2). The nether Beth-horon: it lies about 12 km northwest of Jerusalem (ch. 10:10). Baal: also called Jearim, one of the cities in the portion of Judah and near Jerusalem (ch. 15:9). The well of the waters of Nephtoah: it lies northwest of Jerusalem (ch. 15:9). The valley of the son of Hinnom: it lies south and west of Jerusalem (ch. 15:8), and north of it live the Rephaim and south of it the Jebusites, who are among the original inhabitants of the land.

Geliloth: it is the same as Gilgal, their first center before Shiloh (ch. 4:19). The shoulder: a projection in the high land lying north of the Arabah, that is, the valley (ch. 15:6). The location of the tribe of Benjamin was fixed as a peacemaker between the two quarreling tribes, Ephraim in the north and Judah in the south, and God gave it a small land according to its number, but a distinguished one:
1- Because Jerusalem, the city of the great King, lies in it.
2- Because it is high land, so it is easy to defend it with a small number of inhabitants.
3- It is surrounded by hills that make access to it difficult and under watch.

Therefore we notice the skill of the sons of Benjamin in fighting and in archery, as will appear in the battles of the Book of Judges (ch. 20). The borders of Benjamin were the Jordan River on the east, as far as its mouth into the Dead Sea, and on the west the portion of the tribe of Dan, on the north the portion of the tribe of Ephraim, and on the south the portion of the tribe of Judah. The cities mentioned here were mentioned in (ch. 15) because they are the same as the borders of the tribe of Judah (Map 8). It is to be noted that the tribe of Benjamin lies beside Shiloh, which lies in the tribe of Ephraim, where the tabernacle of meeting was, then in the days of David the tabernacle was moved to Jerusalem, which lies in the portion of the tribe of Benjamin. In this the prophecy of Moses in his blessing of the tribe of Benjamin is fulfilled, where he said “The beloved of the Lord shall dwell in safety by him) ”... Deut 33:12.(
I wish you would be a peacemaker in your place among everyone, so that you are called a son of God (Mt 5:9).

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Simeon

paragraphs.text: When the portion of Judah was determined, it was found to be too large for the tribe, so a part of its portion was taken for the tribe of Simeon.

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Simeon

paragraphs.text: The number of the cities of Simeon was thirteen, because Beersheba and Sheba are two names for one city, and Beersheba had been part of the portion of Judah and was given to his brother Simeon (ch. 15:28).

entries.section: (1) The portion of the tribe of Simeon

paragraphs.text: Thus the borders of the portion of Simeon are, on the east and north, the portion of Judah, on the west the Mediterranean Sea, and on the south the last border of the land of the Jews (Map 8).

The tribe of Judah gave a part of its portion to the tribe of Simeon, and this shows the love among the tribes and the submission to the leader or servant, who is Joshua. Share your livelihood with the needy so that you may be satisfied together by God's graces, and submit to the Head of the Church, Christ, who gave His life on the Cross out of love for us, so that your love increases every day toward those around you.

entries.section: (2) The portion of the tribe of Zebulun

paragraphs.text: The portion included the area bounded on the east by the Lake of Tiberias, on the north by the portions of Naphtali and Asher, on the west by the portion of Asher, and on the south by the portion of Issachar. It includes the city of Nazareth and Mount Tabor (the Transfiguration), and a city named Bethlehem of Zebulun, which is different from the Bethlehem of Judah, the birthplace of Christ, and Gath-hepher (the town of Jonah the prophet). Its land was very fertile, and the main trade route called the Way of the Sea, coming from the Mediterranean to the east, passed through its land (Map 8).

If the tribes took care to possess their portion in the land of Canaan, I wish you would take care of your heavenly portion, which all the good things of the earth signify; as for the good things of your heavenly portion, they cannot be expressed, and you can know something of them through the experience of prayer and contemplation, so that your soul finds rest and rejoices.

entries.section: (3) The portion of the tribe of Issachar

paragraphs.text: The portion of the tribe of Issachar is bounded on the east by the Jordan River, on the north by the portion of Zebulun, and on the west and south by the portion of the western half tribe of Manasseh. In it is the city of Nain, where Christ raised the son of the widow; and it includes the plain of Jezreel, which extends from the Jordan River to the Mediterranean Sea, and its land is distinguished by fertility (Map 8). King Ahab lived in the city of Jezreel, where he took the vineyard of Naboth the Jezreelite, and in it is the city of Shunem, where the Shunammite woman lived in the days of Elisha the prophet (2 Kgs 4).

God has given you a portion in this life that includes various gifts and abilities, which are signified by these cities that the tribe of Issachar possessed. I wish you would use these abilities for the glory of God and be faithful in them, because you are a steward in them for their Owner, who is God, to whom you will give an account of your stewardship on the last day.

entries.section: (4) The portion of the tribe of Asher

paragraphs.text: It is bounded on the east by the portion of the tribe of Naphtali, on the north by the border of the land of the Jews, on the west by the Mediterranean Sea, and on the south by the portions of Zebulun and the western half of Manasseh. Its land is fertile and has minerals such as iron and copper in the northern part. From it came Anna the prophetess (Lk 2:36) and Deborah the judge (Judg 5:17). Its portion includes the city of Cana of Galilee, where Christ turned the water into wine (Jn 2:1-12), and it also includes Mount Carmel, which lies beside the Mediterranean Sea and is mentioned often in the life of the prophets Elijah and Elisha (1 Kgs 18, 2 Kgs 2, 4). Beside it were the possessions of Nabal the Carmelite, the husband of Abigail, who lived in the days of David the prophet (1 Sam 25) (Map 8).

Thank God every day for His gifts to you, that you may feel His fatherhood and love and enjoy the delight of life in His hands, for the greatness of these lands that the tribe of Asher possessed is that they are from the hand of God.

entries.section: (5) The portion of the tribe of Naphtali

paragraphs.text: It is bounded on the east by the Jordan River at its springs, on the north by the border of the land of the Jews, on the west by the portion of the tribe of Asher, and on the south by the portion of the tribe of Zebulun (Map 8). In it is the city of Capernaum, in whose synagogue Christ preached and in which He performed His miracles, and the city of Chorazin (Lk 10:13, 15). And Kedesh in Naphtali, where Barak lived (Judg 4:6). And Tobit lived in the land of Naphtali before he was taken captive to Nineveh (Tob 1).

God promised His people that He would give them the land of Canaan, and here He now divides the land for them by the hand of their leader Joshua. So be confident of God's promises to you and that He will surely fulfill them, however long the time and however adverse the circumstances that surround you.

entries.section: (6) The portion of the tribe of Dan

paragraphs.text: The coast of the children of Dan went out too little for them (v. 47): the Amorites seized a part of the portion of the children of Dan.

Dan was the largest of the tribes in number after Judah, and its original portion was beside the tribe of Judah, bounded on the east by the portion of Benjamin, on the north by the portion of Ephraim, on the west by the Mediterranean Sea, and on the south by the portion of Judah (Map 8). But the Amorites drove them out of some of their portion (v. 47), so they sent to search for another suitable land to take (Judg 18:2-10), and indeed they took Laish, which is Leshem (v. 47), and what is around it, which lies in the northeast of the land of the Jews, where the sources of the Jordan River are, beside Mount Hermon, which is today Mount Sheikh. The incident of the tribe of Dan's taking possession of these regions was mentioned in (Judg 18), and these events took place a little after the death of Joshua, and this incident was probably added here by the hand of Samuel the prophet, because Joshua had died.

The tribe of Dan did not surrender to the pagan inhabitants of the land seizing part of their land, but fought and possessed another part in the north. So do not surrender to the devil's wars, but resist him by the power of God, and He will give you victory over him and will give you all your spiritual needs.

After Joshua completed the distribution of the land to the tribes, he took his portion, which is the city of Timnath-serah, lying north of the mountains of Ephraim. This shows Joshua's love and care for his people before himself, and his humility, which is a type of the humble Christ in His Incarnation and His care for the salvation of His children, whatever it cost of self-giving.
With this the division of the land ended, and each one received his portion that God had determined for him.

I wish you would put others before yourself in honor and earthly good things; then you receive spiritual blessings that cannot be expressed on earth and in heaven, and if you need material blessings, God pours them out on you generously. The cities of refuge. The chapter speaks about the six cities of refuge and their law, as previously in the Book of Numbers (ch. 35); three cities were fixed east of the Jordan and three west of it, so that the one fleeing to them from any place in the country would not travel more than thirty miles.

entries.section: (1) The law of the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: The Lord asked Joshua to appoint the cities of refuge to guarantee the right of one who killed unintentionally not to be killed, as God had made clear earlier to Moses in (Num 35:9-15, Deut 19:2-10). These cities lie among the cities of the Levites, because they live among the tribes, so it is easy for the killer to take refuge in them and be under the care of God's servants the Levites.

entries.section: (1) The law of the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: The way of flight to those cities was easy because of the good distribution of their locations. They would prepare the roads leading to them and put crossings over the rivers so that the fugitive would find no obstacles on the way, for he is innocent and did not intend to kill, so he escapes from the avenger of blood, that is, the relative of the killer who wants to take vengeance for him. As for the one who kills deliberately, he has no place in these cities and deserves death.

entries.section: (1) The law of the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: When the one who killed unintentionally reaches the city of refuge, he stands at its gate and presents his case before the elders of the city; if they are convinced of his innocence, they allow him to stay in it and do not hand him over to the relatives of the one killed, but protect him from their vengeance.

entries.section: (1) The law of the cities of refuge

paragraphs.text: After the elders of the city judge him innocent, he dwells in the city until he stands before the elders of the congregation of the children of Israel to examine his case and confirm his innocence; then he returns to the city of refuge he had entered, and stays there until the death of the great priest, that is, the high priest, and then returns with honor to his city, and none of the relatives of the one killed unintentionally can molest him, or else he will be punished. Thus he has received the penalty for his carelessness and the unintentional killing, which is to be away from his city and family during his stay in the city of refuge.
The great priest is a type of Christ, by whose death we received salvation.

God's mercies are great, for He makes allowance for the one who killed unintentionally and gives him life and safety in the city of refuge. I wish you would make allowance for everyone who wrongs you and forgive him, so that you give him a new opportunity to live with God and with you in love.
They sanctified: that is, they set apart and dedicated.
Kedesh: it lies in the portion of the tribe of Naphtali in Galilee and is different from Kadesh-barnea.

Shechem: it lies in the middle of the land of Canaan and is present-day Nabulus, 50 km north of Jerusalem. Kirjath-arba: it is the one that Caleb the son of Jephunneh possessed and is now called Al-Khalil.
The stranger: those who are not Jews living with them.

Three cities were chosen west of the Jordan River: Kedesh in the north, Shechem in the middle and Hebron in the south; and three other cities east of the Jordan River: Bezer in the south, Ramoth in the middle and Golan in the north. Moses had appointed them (Deut 4:41-43), to be used to give the opportunity of escape to every one who killed unintentionally, whether of the Jews or of the strangers living among them (Map 9). Golan, Ramoth. Map (9) Cities of refuge
The Lord calls us to take refuge in Him from the divine wrath by repentance, opening His arms to receive us; will we refuse the invitation or welcome it?

The cities of the priests and the Levites. In this chapter are determined the cities of the priests and the Levites that were given to them by God's command, with their pastures, so that they might live in them in the midst of the people without leaving them.

We notice that the priests, that is, the descendants of Aaron, and the three families of the Levites, that is, the Kohathites, the Gershonites and the Merarites, each received a fixed share of these cities.
Suburbs: pastures.

The Levites asked for the cities of their portion, and God gave them by lot, and so they took what suffices for their dwelling needs and the pasture of their cattle from the portion of the tribes, whether east of the Jordan or west of it.

I wish we would give to each one according to what God has given us of blessing and abundance, so that our possessions are blessed by this giving, and our love toward others is established, and we feel our oneness in Christ.

Most of the cities of the priests were concentrated in the southern region of Canaan, which would become the southern kingdom in the future, because God knows that the Temple and the service of the priests would be in this region. The priests were of the sons of the Kohathites, of the descendants of Aaron (1 Chr 6:1-3).

God's ordering of your life now may not be understood at present, but the time will come when you will know that it was the best choice at its time, for God loves you and chooses for you everything that gives you rest and brings you to the Kingdom.

entries.section: (3) The rest of the portion of the Kohathites and the portion of the Gershonites and the portion of the Merarites

paragraphs.text: The total of the cities of the Levites and priests was 48 cities with their pastures, among them six cities of refuge. Thus the servants were spread out in the midst of the people without isolation so that they could lead and guide them easily, as Christ shared with us by His Incarnation and dwelling in our midst.

The Levites did not take a portion like the rest of the tribes, but God gave them cities to dwell in, because God is their portion, since they were consecrated to His service. The cities in which they lived were 48 cities, which is more than the portion of most of the other tribes, for God gives His servants spiritual blessings and suffices all their material needs. So offer your love to God and serve Him faithfully, trusting in His care, which suffices your needs and even distinguishes you from those around you, so that your thanks and your service to Him increase.

entries.section: (4) The completion of the distribution of the land

paragraphs.text: God fulfilled His promise to His children by giving them the land of Canaan that He had promised them, and gave them victory over all their enemies and subdued them to them, as a type of Christ's victory on the Cross and the subjection of Satan under our feet.

Trust in the power of God that supports you and gives you victory over your enemies the demons, however great your weakness and however great the power of the demons, because God loves you and keeps you from all evil as long as you hold fast to Him.
The return to the east of the Jordan and the new altar

Joshua called the men of war of the tribe of Reuben and Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh to thank them for keeping their covenant with Moses (Num 32) and their obedience to him in accompanying their brothers for about seven years to possess the lands west of the Jordan.

He praised their holding fast to helping their brothers until they took possession of their portion west of the Jordan. And he allowed the warriors to return to their homes, and their number was about 40,000 fighters. We notice that the Jews sometimes lived in tents even after their settling in the land of Canaan, and they often pitched their tents and stayed in them, especially in the summer season, in addition to pitching them beside their fields to take care of them; and at first they pitched tents beside the houses of the original inhabitants because those had been destroyed and needed rebuilding or repair.
He commanded them to keep obeying God's commandments and to love Him and worship Him with all the heart, then sent them away with a blessing.

They returned laden with blessings to their land, that is, the spoils they had taken from the original inhabitants of the land after they triumphed over them with their brothers of the rest of the tribes. And they divided these spoils with their brothers who had remained to guard the homes east of the Jordan, according to the law of war, while the rest of the tribe of Manasseh took its portion west of the Jordan.

After God gives you victory over your enemies the demons, do not grow slack in your spiritual worship, but thank God and enjoy being in His hands, because His love is the goal of your life and it is what protects you from Satan.

The region of Jordan: the Jordan River curves north of the Dead Sea so that it becomes in the shape of an arc and then continues its course to the north, so the shape of this region lying east of the Jordan is nearly a circle. After the children of Reuben and the children of Gad and the half tribe of Manasseh crossed the Jordan River and reached the east of the Jordan River, they built a great altar in this part of the curved land that resembles a peninsula. That is, they built it in their possession east of the Jordan to remember God's altar. Of course they could not build it west of the Jordan, because there the tabernacle of meeting was at Shiloh, and the altar was in it, so there was no need to build altars to remember God's altars, since it was easy for them to reach the tabernacle of meeting if they were west of the Jordan.

The news of the building of this new altar reached the rest of the tribes of the children of Israel, and they were greatly enraged and considered that the two and a half tribes living east of the Jordan had apostatized from the faith in God by building an altar east of the Jordan opposite the land of Canaan.
The tribes decided to fight the two and a half tribes, and the men of the tribes assembled at Shiloh, where God's altar was, declaring their holding fast to the worship of God in His house.
I wish you would make clear the meaning of your words and actions so that others do not understand them in the opposite way, and so you gain your peace and theirs.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: House: tribe.
Father: that is, the sons of Jacob from whom the tribes came.
Thousands of Israel: the people of Israel, who are counted by thousands.

In an attempt at understanding before the war, the people sent a delegation headed by Phinehas the priest, known for his zeal (Num 25:7-13), with ten chiefs for the nine and a half tribes in the west, to negotiate with the sons of the east in Gilead.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: The delegation declared its objection to the betrayal of the Lord by making a strange altar, although God had forbidden this (Lev 17:8-9) when He commanded them to offer their sacrifices on one altar, which is the one in the tabernacle of meeting.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: They reminded them of what happened as a result of Balaam's counsel to Balak (Num 25:1-3), of the young men of the people being made to stumble into adultery with the Moabite women in the region of Peor, the god of the children of Ammon, a matter that they remember with sorrow to this very time because many fell dead by the plague. Thus this altar of theirs would bring harm upon the whole people.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: The land of the possession of the Lord ... wherein the Lord's tabernacle dwelleth: what is meant is the land of Canaan west of the Jordan.

They offered them to move and dwell with them in the west if they considered that the land of the east was unclean because there was no altar of the Lord in it, and to cease this rebellion of building a strange altar. They also made them understand how the sin of Achan harmed the whole people and caused the death of many besides him (ch. 7), that is, they warned them that the building of this altar would bring God's wrath upon all the children of Israel.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: The reply of the eastern tribes to the delegation affirmed that there was no intention of betrayal, and held fast to the declaration of their faith in God by the names by which He is known in their Hebrew language, that is, the Lord God of gods, and they repeated this for emphasis and to call the Lord to witness His knowledge of their intentions and their not betraying.
Save us not this day: they do not deserve salvation, but punishment from God, if they intend betrayal.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: They said that the reason for building this great stone altar was not to offer sacrifices on it apart from the altar of the Lord, or else let God punish them. But the reason was their fear that the sons of the western tribes might think in the future that the sons of the eastern tribes are not Jews and do not know God, and might prevent them from taking part in the Jewish feasts in the house of the Lord.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: And the existence of the Jordan valley, whose depth is about 3,000 to 4,000 feet, would confirm their supposition that the sons of the east are strangers, so they would prevent them from worshiping God, and consequently they would lose their fear of God and be attached to the worship of idols.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: God forbid that we should: a declaration of their rejection of the evil intention of betraying God and offering sacrifices on another altar.

They declared that their purpose in building this great altar was not to use it for offering burnt offerings and sacrifices on it, but to proclaim their faith in God's altar and His worship, and that they would offer their burnt offerings and sacrifices before it, that is, on God's altar in His house at Shiloh or afterwards at Jerusalem, since its shape and likeness to the altar of burnt offering would confirm their relationship with the Lord. In this way they affirmed that there was no betrayal of God in their hearts or in their conduct, and that sacrifices would be offered only on the one altar of the Lord before the tabernacle of meeting.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: The words pleased Phinehas and the delegation, and they were convinced of their faithfulness and thanked them for it.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: Phinehas and the delegation returned to the lands west of the Jordan and told the people what had happened, and everyone was convinced by the words and approved them, and gave up their thought of fighting their brothers.

entries.section: (3) An accepted apology and a true witness

paragraphs.text: A witness: a testimony.
The sons of the east called the altar a witness because it is a witness between them and their brothers to their faith that the Lord is God.
And perhaps this altar signified:
1- The return of the Jews to the Christian faith in the last days.

2- The altar of the Jews after the coming of Christ and His crucifixion, which became an altar without function or meaning. It is noticed that the half tribe of Manasseh was not mentioned at the end of the speech, as a kind of brevity.

I wish you would not be hasty in judging others, and would try to reach an understanding with them or reproach them so that you may clarify the truth and overcome with love all the thoughts of the devil.

Joshua's farewell address. This chapter and the one that follows it are Joshua's last speech to the people and his handing the trust over to them and bidding them farewell after advising and guiding them.

entries.section: (1) The summoning of the leaders to hear the address

paragraphs.text: A long time: after the passing of several years.
Officers: the plural of "officer," meaning an overseer or a deputy of the people.

After a period of time, when the wars of Canaan had ended and Joshua had grown old, Joshua called the people and their leaders in order to give them his charge and bid them farewell in his old age. This gathering was most likely at the place where he lived, in Timnath-serah, or in Shiloh before the tabernacle of meeting. Here we notice the concern of the faithful servant Joshua to sum up his counsel to his children in a farewell address, as Moses did (Deut 29-31) and as Samuel did (1 Sam 12).

entries.section: (1) The summoning of the leaders to hear the address

paragraphs.text: Joshua did not attribute the victories to himself but to the Lord, who gave them to the people and who fought for His people. He made them understand that he had divided the land among them by lot, according to the Lord's choice of the place of each tribe, so that they would not quarrel after his death, from the banks of the Jordan River in the east to the Mediterranean Sea in the west, as was explained before.

Be careful to offer counsel to those in your care, so that you encourage them to live with God and to stand firm in the faith. Fulfill what you feel God asks of you, and your heart will be at rest. Trust that He will help you in this striving of yours and will give you grace in the eyes of those around you.
Come not among these nations: do not mingle with them.

The Lord had promised them the land, and He Himself drives out its inhabitants from before them, but they must hold fast to carrying out God's commandments, which the prophet Moses taught them and wrote in his books. This shows us the importance of handing down the faith and Christian conduct from generation to generation according to God's commandment, without deviation to the right through excess and exaggeration, or to the left through neglecting them. The children of Israel did carry out Joshua's words at times, and they drove out some of the pagan peoples in the days of the Judges, but they were slack in driving out the others, so these peoples became a snare to them and drew them into the worship of idols.

They must not mingle with the pagan peoples who dwelt in the land before them, nor with those who remained among them, nor mention the names of their gods, lest they become attached to them by swearing by their names, or worship them, or bow down to them. Rather, they were to cleave to the Lord, as they had done during the days of Joshua's life among them.

Since the Lord drove out from before them strong and great nations, so that no man stood against them, let them know that God's help to man is the secret of man's strength. God multiplies the strength of one so that he chases a thousand; He is the One who works in us as long as we love Him and believe in Him as King and God.
Here the importance of encouragement appears, so make your tongue sweet and encouraging to those you deal with, so that you may strengthen their weakness and draw them to Christ.

He warns them against turning back from the way of the Lord and entering into relationships, dealings and intermarriage with the pagan peoples, for the mother is the child's first educator, and it is she who plants faith in him. If a person is careless in this, God withdraws His help from him, and these wicked people hunt him down for evil like a snare that Satan uses to trap him. Then the person suffers from the conduct and errors that the wicked plant in him, until they themselves turn into a wicked people whom God destroys, as He destroyed the pagans who were before them. So the stumbling that the pagans would cause the Jews is likened to a snare into which the prey falls, or a thorn in the eye that prevents it from seeing so that it goes astray, or a whip that inflicts very painful lashes on a person.

Joshua announced to them that he was near the end of his life on earth, as will happen to every person, assuring them that the Lord's counsels of blessing for them are true, as has been proven in practice by their victories and their possession of the land. His threat of punishment is also true if they turn away from God, until the matter ends in their destruction from the land if they persist in transgressing God's good commandments, betraying His covenant and turning to the worship of other gods; then God's wrath will move against them severely and they will be destroyed. This happened in the captivity of the children of Israel at the hands of Assyria and then Babylon.

The servant has one role to encourage the weak and another necessary role to warn the careless, so that he may hold to God's law and love. So do not hesitate to show the truth in the manner suited to each of those for whom you are responsible, so that you draw all to God and keep them away from evil.
The last message here is God's last message to the people through Joshua.
Shechem: the present-day city of Nablus. It lies on the west bank of the Jordan, in the portion of the western half-tribe of Manasseh (Map 5), and it has good spiritual memories:
1- There God gave Abraham the first promise, and he built the first altar to the Lord (Gen 12:6, 7).
2- There the blessings and the curses were read to the people from Mount Gerizim and Mount Ebal.
3- In it were buried the bones of Joseph, which they had carried with them at the Exodus from Egypt, when they entered the Promised Land (Josh 8:30-35).
4- There Joshua read the law of the Lord to the people (ch. 8:30). The flood: the River Euphrates.

Joshua gathered the people a second time at Shechem with their leaders and representatives, and they came to a holy assembly in the presence of God to hear the message directed to them from the Lord through Joshua's tongue, in which Joshua reviewed their whole history with God and all His support of them, from the call of Abraham from beyond the River Euphrates in Iraq, to leave the worship of idols that his family practiced and turn to the worship of God.

God chose Abraham and brought him to the land of Canaan and gave him a blessed offspring through Isaac, whom He granted him in his old age. Isaac begot Jacob and Esau. Because Esau was occupied with material desires, God gave him Mount Seir, and he dwelt in it and turned away from the spiritual life with God, while Jacob and his sons went down to Egypt (Gen 45:9, 10; 46:2-10), so that God might train them in the spiritual life through humiliation and hardship, and then faith and trust.

Moses and Aaron came and struck Egypt with the ten plagues until Pharaoh allowed the people to go out. They went out and came to the Red Sea, and God parted it for them and drowned the Egyptians in it when they tried to pursue them in order to seize them.

And he put darkness between you and the Egyptians: so that God might protect His people crossing the Red Sea from the Egyptians who were following them, He moved the pillar of fire from before the children of Israel to behind them, and it separated the Egyptians from the children of Israel. By the power and size of the fire, the Egyptians' sight was blocked and they could no longer see the children of Israel, so the fire was like darkness until all the children of Israel had crossed and come out of the sea. God hid His people from Pharaoh until the children of Israel came to the wilderness of Sinai, and He was glorified in His care for them. When they came to the land of the Amorites, they took their land. God did not allow Balaam to curse them but made him bless them; Balak king of Moab had brought him to curse the children of Israel, and God delivered them from his hand (Num 22, 23, 24). Joshua's saying "your eyes have seen" refers to the elderly and the older ones among them who witnessed these events even as children with their fathers.
The land of the Amorites: it lies east of the Jordan River.

Then they crossed the Jordan, and their wars with the Canaanite peoples began, with the fighting against Jericho and their capture of it, and then the wars of the west bank of the Jordan, which lasted about seven years, and their victory in them.
Hornets: stinging insects.

Here God announces the fulfillment of His promise to Moses to send the hornets to help His people in their war against the enemies (Ex 23:28; Deut 7:20). He sent them before the children of Israel when they fought the Amorites east of the Jordan River, so the enemies feared and fled, and God's people did not need to use their weapons to drive out the enemies, since God drove them out of the land by the stings of the hornets. So they received their land ready for habitation, with its cities and its crops, to enjoy.
May you review God's works with you so that you thank Him for them and your faith is thereby confirmed, and you are reassured and rejoice in His care for you.

Because of the greatness of God's work with His people, they must fear Him and serve Him faithfully, and abandon the remnants of idol worship that they practiced on the journey through the wilderness and that their forefathers had practiced earlier in Iraq, by the River Euphrates, before God's call to Abraham, and reject the gods of the Amorites, whose lands the Lord gave them as an inheritance.

Joshua asks them whether they want to serve God or to leave Him and serve the idols. In this he stirs them up so that they decide to serve God and do not halt between the two ways, that is, the worship of God and the worship of idols. He set himself forth as an example, for he resolved that he and his household would serve God and not the idols.
It is good for the servant to be an example to those he serves, giving them the good example whose steps they follow.

entries.section: (2) The people's covenant to serve God

paragraphs.text: The people answered that it was impossible for them to leave the worship of God after what He had done for them.

For He is the One who rescued them from the bondage of Pharaoh in Egypt, preserved them by miracles on the journey through the wilderness, saved them from their enemies, drove them out before them and gave them their land as an inheritance. Therefore they were determined to worship Him as their God.

entries.section: (2) The people's covenant to serve God

paragraphs.text: Joshua wanted to make clear to them that the commitment to worship the Lord must be complete. It is not easy, because God is holy and jealous for His name, and He does not forgive those who betray Him, turn away from worshiping Him and turn to worship another; rather, He punishes them and destroys them if they do so, because He wants the whole heart and the whole intention, not a part of them. Joshua wanted his people to know the obligations of life with God so as to enjoy all His blessings, just as Christ asked us to count the cost, that is, to carry His cross behind us so that we may enjoy His care and be sons of the Kingdom.

entries.section: (2) The people's covenant to serve God

paragraphs.text: The people affirmed to Joshua their adherence to the worship of God, with insistence and repetition. Joshua made them witnesses against themselves, and they testified. He asked them to put away the strange gods from among them, that is, the statues of the gods that they still kept in their houses, so that their hearts would be wholly directed to God, and they promised him to obey God. Our father Jacob did this when he returned from his uncle Laban: he buried them and got rid of them, proving his good intention in worshiping God (Gen 33:18-20; 35:2).

entries.section: (2) The people's covenant to serve God

paragraphs.text: A statute and an ordinance: what is meant is commitment to the covenant, that is, worshiping God and obeying His commandments.
The book of the law of God: the Book of Joshua is considered an extension of the five books of the Law that Moses wrote, so it was also called the book of the law of God.

Joshua made a covenant between the people and God and bound them to obey this covenant, that is, to worship God. Joshua recorded these words in this book of his, that is, the Book of Joshua, as part of the divine Law. He set up a great stone that was there in the place, under the oak at Shechem, which is considered a holy place. The stone is a symbol of Christ, the Rock of Ages, on whom, if the house is founded, it will never fall, however great the storms and tempests.

entries.section: (2) The people's covenant to serve God

paragraphs.text: Deny: disown.

Joshua made the stone, which had been present for the words and had heard them, a witness against the people so that they would be committed to worshiping God. Then Joshua sent the people away to their dwelling places.

Examine yourself to know the goal of your life and to measure your steps, whether you are walking toward it or deviating from it into many sins, and if you have deviated, return to God by repentance, that is, remind yourself every day of your goal, which is the love of God.

entries.section: (3) The death of Joshua and Eleazar, and the bones of Joseph

paragraphs.text: Border: boundaries.

After Joshua bade farewell to his people and gave them his final commandments, he died at the age of one hundred and twenty years and was buried in the land of his inheritance in the city of Timnath-heres, which lies in the portion of Ephraim (Map 12). These last verses were written by someone other than Joshua, most likely the prophet Samuel, the writer of the Book of Judges.

entries.section: (3) The death of Joshua and Eleazar, and the bones of Joseph

paragraphs.text: The people continued in the worship of God in the days of Joshua and in the days of the elders who were contemporary with him, who had witnessed God's work in the entering of the land, and whose lives were long after Joshua's death.

entries.section: (3) The death of Joshua and Eleazar, and the bones of Joseph

paragraphs.text: Piece of money: a coin whose value is not known.
The hill of Phinehas: the name of a city of the priests in the portion of the tribe of Ephraim.
Mount Gaash: a mountain near the city of Timnath-serah.

Joseph had died in Egypt and had charged the children of Israel to carry his bones with them when they went out. Joseph's death was more than two hundred years before Joshua's birth, so they took his bones when they went out and buried them in Shechem, the land that his father Jacob had earlier bought from the sons of Hamor when he returned to the land of Canaan from his uncle Laban (Gen 33:19).

entries.section: (3) The death of Joshua and Eleazar, and the bones of Joseph

paragraphs.text: Eleazar: a Hebrew name meaning "God helps."
Then Eleazar the high priest, the son of Aaron, died and was buried in the hill of Phinehas his son, which is one of the cities of the priests in the portion of the tribe of Ephraim.
We received the right to our heavenly inheritance when our High Priest Jesus died, our Leader on our journey, so let us thank God for this inheritance that does not perish and rejoice in it.

Joshua is a type of Christ. (1) He shares the name with Christ, for both names derive from "Yehoshua," which means the Lord is Savior. (2) The crossing: Joshua crossed with the people over the Jordan River when he parted it by the entry of the priests carrying the ark of the covenant of the Lord, and so he brought the people over to the new life in the Promised Land. Christ by His redemption brought us over from subjection to sin and the age of the Law to the new life with Him in His Church, in which we receive the sacrament of Baptism. As the people were baptized with Joshua in the Jordan, so we receive salvation in the sacrament of Baptism.
(3) The inheritance: as Joshua gave the land of Canaan and divided it among the tribes, so Christ gives us our eternal inheritance in the heavenly Canaan, that is, the Kingdom of Heaven.

(4) The commandments: Joshua was careful to charge his people to live with God and affirmed this in his farewell address at the end of the book, and Christ also gave His commandments so that His people might live by them.

(5) The covenant: Joshua made a covenant between God and His people before he died, so that they might live with God and keep His commandments, and Christ made a covenant between us and God by His blood on the cross, and gives us this covenant in His Church through its Holy Sacraments.

(6) Freedom: after Joshua charged his people, he left them free to choose the worship of God or the worship of idols, and they chose God. In the same way Christ also respected man's freedom and said, "He that hath ears to hear, let him hear" (Mt 11:15), or "Whoever wants to accept, let him accept."

(7) Miracles: God confirmed Joshua's teachings with miracles, such as the parting of the Jordan River (ch. 2) and the stopping of the sun and the moon during the fight against the enemies (ch. 10:12, 13). Christ confirmed His teachings with many miracles, such as healing the sick, raising the dead, casting out demons and His authority over nature. (8) The farewell address: Joshua gave his last instructions before his death in a farewell address at the end of the book, and Christ gave a farewell address to His disciples, which is recorded in (Jn 14-16). (9) Victory: Joshua triumphed over his enemies, whether in the wilderness of Sinai, as in his victory over Amalek (Ex 17), or in the land of Canaan, whose land he possessed, and Christ triumphed over Satan in the temptation on the mountain, then bound him by His cross and gave his place in heaven to those who believe in Him.
